For those capable of being taught, the penetration of knowledge and the attainment of arahantship occur to that extent, because they are to be realized by emerging from these.

Dassanapariṇāyakaṭṭhenāti andhassa yaṭṭhikoṭiṃ gahetvā maggadesako viya dhammānaṃ yathāsabhāvadassanasaṅkhātena pariṇāyakabhāvena. Yathā vā so tassa cakkhubhūto, evaṃ sattānaṃ paññā. Tenāha “cakkhubhūtāya paññāyā”ti. Samādhisampayuttā paññā samādhipaññā. Samādhi cettha āruppasamādhīti vadanti, sammasanapayogo pana koci jhānasamādhīti yuttaṃ. Vipassanābhūtā paññā vipassanāpaññā. Samādhipaññāya antosamāpattiyaṃ kiccato pajānāti, “samāhito yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī”ti pana vacanato (saṃ. ni. 3.5; 4.99-100; 3.5.1071-1072; netti. 40; mi. pa. 2.1.14) asammohato pajānāti. Tattha kiccatoti gocarajjhatte ārammaṇakaraṇakiccato. Asammohatoti sampayuttadhammesu sammohavidhamanato yathā pītipaṭisaṃvedanādīsu. Kimatthiyāti kiṃpayojanāti āha “ko etissā attho”ti. Abhiññeyye dhammeti yāthāvasarasalakkhaṇāvabodhavasena abhimukhaṃ ñeyye jānitabbe khandhāyatanādidhamme. Abhijānātīti salakkhaṇato sāmaññalakkhaṇato ca abhimukhaṃ avirajjhanavasena jānāti. Etena ñātapariññābyāpāramāha. Pariññeyyeti aniccātipi dukkhātipi anattātipi paricchijja jānitabbe. Parijānātīti “yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ…pe… aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhenā”tiādinā (paṭi. ma. 1.48) paricchinditvā jānāti. Iminā tīraṇapariññābyāpāramāha. Pahātabbe dhammeti niccasaññādike yāva arahattamaggavajjhā sabbe pāpadhamme. Pajahati pakaṭṭhato jahati, vikkhambheti ceva samucchindati cāti attho. Iminā pahānapariññābyāpāramāha. Sā panesā paññā lokiyāpi tippakārā lokuttarāpi, tāsaṃ visesaṃ sayamevāha. Kiccatoti abhijānanavasena ārammaṇakiccato. Asammohatoti yathābalaṃ abhiññeyyādīsu sammohavidhamanato. Nibbānamārammaṇaṃ katvā pavattanato abhiññeyyādīsu vigatasammohato evāti āha “lokuttarā asammohato”ti.

'By the characteristic of being a guide to vision' means that just as a guide takes the end of a staff to show the path to a blind person, so too is wisdom a guide by way of seeing the true nature of phenomena. And just as that person becomes the eye for the blind, so too does wisdom for beings. Hence it is said, 'wisdom that has become the eye.' Wisdom associated with concentration is concentration-wisdom. Here, some say that concentration refers to the formless attainments, but it is fitting to say that the application of thorough investigation is jhāna-concentration. Wisdom that is insight is insight-wisdom. Concentration-wisdom understands by way of its function within the attainment; but, according to the statement, 'one who is concentrated understands as it really is,' it understands without confusion. There, 'by function' means by performing its function of making an object in its sphere of operation. 'Without delusion' means by dispelling delusion regarding associated phenomena, such as the experience of rapture, etc. 'Kimatthiyā' (for what purpose?) means 'what is its benefit?'. Hence it is said, 'What is its purpose?'. 'Phenomena to be directly known' refers to the aggregates, sense bases, etc., which are to be known directly by way of comprehending their own characteristics as they truly are. 'Directly knows' means knowing without failing by recognizing their specific and general characteristics. This indicates the function of the comprehension of knowledge. 'To be fully understood' means to be known by discerning them as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. 'Fully understands' means knowing by discerning them as, 'whatever form there is... is impermanent in the sense of destruction,' etc. (Paṭisambhidāmagga 1.48). This indicates the function of the comprehension of scrutiny. 'Phenomena to be abandoned' refers to all evil phenomena, from perceptions of permanence up to those abandoned by the Arahant path. 'Abandons' means it abandons completely; the meaning is that it suppresses and eradicates. This indicates the function of the comprehension of abandoning. This wisdom is mundane and supramundane, and of three kinds. Its distinctions are explained by himself. 'By function' means by its function of making an object by way of directly knowing. 'Without delusion' means by dispelling delusion regarding what is to be directly known, etc., according to its power. Because it proceeds having Nibbāna as its object, it is indeed free from delusion regarding what is to be directly known, etc. Hence it is said, 'supramundane, because of being without delusion.'

452. Kammassakatā [M 2.0268][V 2.0248] sammādiṭṭhi ca vaṭṭanissitattā idha nādhippetā, vivaṭṭakathā hesāti vuttaṃ “vipassanāsammādiṭṭhiyā ca maggasammādiṭṭhiyā cā”ti. Parato ghosoti parato satthuto, sāvakato vā labbhamāno dhammaghoso. Tenāha “sappāyadhammassavana”nti. Tañhi sammādiṭṭhiyā paccayo bhavituṃ sakkoti, na yo koci paratoghoso. Upāyamanasikāroti yena nāmarūpapariggahādi sijjhati, tādiso pathamanasikāro. Ayañca sammādiṭṭhiyā paccayoti niyamapakkhiko, na sabbasaṃgāhakoti dassento “paccekabuddhānaṃ panā”tiādimāha. Yonisomanasikārasmiṃyevāti avadhāraṇena paratoghosameva nivatteti, na padaṭṭhānavisesaṃ paṭiyogīnivattanatthattā eva-saddassa.

452. The right view pertaining to kamma ownership is not intended here because it is dependent on the round of existence; for this is a discussion of liberation from the round. Hence it is said, 'by insight right view and path right view.' 'The voice of another' means the Dhamma-voice received from another, from a teacher or a disciple. Therefore, it is said, 'listening to suitable Dhamma.' For that can indeed become a condition for right view, not just any voice of another. 'Appropriate attention' means such initial attention by which the comprehension of name-and-form, etc., is accomplished. And showing that this is a condition for right view according to a fixed principle, not universally inclusive, he said, 'But for the Paccekabuddhas...' and so on. By the restrictive particle 'eva' in 'only in wise attention,' he excludes only the voice of another, not a specific proximate cause, because the word 'eva' has the meaning of excluding an opposite.

Laddhupakārāti (a. ni. ṭī. 3.5.25) yathārahaṃ nissayādivasena laddhapaccayā. Vipassanāsammādiṭṭhiyā anuggahitabhāvena gahitattā maggasammādiṭṭhīsu ca arahattamaggasammādiṭṭhi, anantarassa hi vidhi, paṭisedho vā. Aggaphalasamādhimhi tapparikkhāradhammesuyeva ca kevalo cetopariyāyo niruḷhoti sammādiṭṭhīti arahattamaggasammādiṭṭhi. Phalakkhaṇeti anantare kālantare cāti duvidhe phalakkhaṇe. Paṭippassaddhivasena sabbasaṃkilesehi ceto vimuccati etāyāti cetovimutti, aggaphalapaññaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā phaladhammā. Tenāha “cetovimutti phalaṃ assāti. Cetovimuttisaṅkhātaṃ phalaṃ ānisaṃso”ti, sabbasaṃkilesehi cetaso vimuccanasaṅkhātaṃ paṭippassambhanasaññitaṃ pahānaṃ phalaṃ ānisaṃso cāti yojanā. Idha ca cetovimutti-saddena pahānamattaṃ gahitaṃ, pubbe pahāyakadhammā, aññathā phaladhammā eva ānisaṃsoti gayhamāne punavacanaṃ niratthakaṃ siyā.

'Laddhupakārā' (A.N. Ṭī. 3.5.25) means having obtained conditions appropriately by way of support, etc. Because it is grasped as being supported by insight right view, and among the path right views, it is the Arahant path right view that is meant here, for there is an injunction or prohibition for what is immediate. In the supreme fruition concentration, only the complete mental penetration arises concerning those supporting factors, and thus it is right view, namely, the Arahant path right view. 'The moment of fruition' refers to the two kinds of fruition moments: the immediate and the subsequent. By way of subsidence, the mind is liberated from all defilements by this, hence it is called 'liberation of mind,' meaning the remaining fruition-states apart from the supreme fruition-wisdom. Hence he said, 'Liberation of mind is its fruition.' The fruition designated as liberation of mind is the benefit. The interpretation is that the abandonment, designated as subsidence, characterized by the mind's liberation from all defilements, is both the fruition and the benefit. And here, by the word 'liberation of mind,' only abandonment is taken, because the phenomena to be abandoned were mentioned previously; otherwise, if the fruition-states themselves were taken as the benefit, the repetition would be meaningless.

Paññāvimuttiphalānisaṃsāti etthāpi evameva attho veditabbo. Sammāvācākammantājīvā sīlasabhāvattā visesato samādhissa upakārā, tathā sammāsaṅkappo jhānasabhāvattā. Tathā hi so “appanā”ti niddiṭṭho. Sammāsatisammāvāyāmā pana samādhipakkhiyā evāti āha “avasesā dhammā cetovimuttīti veditabbā”ti. Catupārisuddhisīlanti ariyamaggādhigamassa padaṭṭhānabhūtaṃ catupārisuddhisīlaṃ. Sutādīsupi eseva nayo. Attano cittappavattiārocanavasena saha kathanaṃ saṃkathā, saṃkathāva [M 2.0269] sākacchā. Idha pana kammaṭṭhānapaṭibaddhāti āha “kammaṭṭhāne…pe… kathā”ti. Tattha kammaṭṭhānassa ekavāraṃ vīthiyā appaṭipajjanaṃ khalanaṃ, anekavāraṃ pakkhalanaṃ, tadubhayassa vicchedanīkathā khalanapakkhalanachedanakathā. Pūrentassāti vivaṭṭanissitaṃ katvā pālentassa brūhentassa ca. Suṇantassāti “yathāuggahitakammaṭṭhānaṃ phātiṃ gamissatī”ti [V 2.0249] evaṃ suṇantassa. Teneva hi “sappāyadhammassavana”nti vuttaṃ. Kammaṃ karontassāti bhāvanānuyogakammaṃ karontassa.

Here too, the meaning of 'the fruition and benefit of liberation by wisdom' should be understood in this same way. Right speech, right action, and right livelihood, because of their nature as virtue, are especially helpful to concentration, just as right intention, because of its nature as jhāna. For it is described as 'full absorption.' Right mindfulness and right effort, however, belong precisely to the side of concentration, hence he said, 'the remaining factors should be understood as mental liberation.' 'The fourfold purified virtue' means the fourfold purified virtue, which is the foundation for attaining the noble path. The same principle applies to learning and so forth. Talking together by way of explaining one's own mental activity is called 'saṃkathā' (conversation); saṃkathā itself is 'sākacchā' (discussion). Here, however, it is connected to the meditation subject, thus he said, '...talk on the meditation subject...' In this context, a single failure of the meditation subject to enter the course is stumbling; repeated failures are slipping; talk that cuts off both is called talk that cuts off stumbling and slipping. 'For one who fulfills' means for one who protects and develops it, having made it dependent on that which turns away from the cycle of rebirth. 'For one who listens' means for one who listens with the thought, 'The meditation subject I have learned will come to fruition.' Therefore, it is called 'listening to suitable Dhamma.' 'For one who practices' means for one who engages in the work of meditative practice.

Pañcasupi ṭhānesu anta-saddo hetuatthajotano daṭṭhabbo. Evañhi “yathā hī”tiādinā vuccamānā ambupamā ca yujjeyya. Udakakoṭṭhakanti ālavālaṃ. Thiraṃ katvā bandhatīti asithilaṃ daḷhaṃ nātimahantaṃ nātikhuddakaṃ katvā yojeti. Thiraṃ karotīti udakasiñcanakāle tato tato vissaritvā udakassa anikkhamanatthaṃ ālavālaṃ thirataraṃ karoti. Sukkhadaṇḍakoti tasseva ambagacchakassa sukkho sākhāsīsako. Kipillikapuṭoti tambakipillikakuṭajaṃ. Khaṇittinti kudālaṃ. Koṭṭhakabandhanaṃ viya sīlaṃ sammādiṭṭhiyā vaḍḍhanupāyassa mūlabhāvato. Udakasiñcanaṃ viya dhammassavanaṃ bhāvanāya paribrūhanato. Mariyādāya thirabhāvakaraṇaṃ viya samatho yathāvuttabhāvanādhiṭṭhānāya sīlamariyādāya daḷhabhāvāpādanato. Samāhitassa hi sīlaṃ thirataraṃ hoti. Samīpe valliādīnaṃ haraṇaṃ viya kammaṭṭhāne khalanapakkhalanacchedanaṃ ijjhitabbabhāvanāya vibandhāpanayanato. Mūlakhaṇanaṃ viya sattannaṃ anupassanānaṃ bhāvanā tassā vibandhassa mūlakānaṃ taṇhāmānadiṭṭhīnaṃ palikhaṇanato. Ettha ca yasmā suparisuddhasīlassa kammaṭṭhānaṃ anuyuñjantassa sappāyadhammassavanaṃ icchitabbaṃ, tato yathāsute atthe sākacchāsamāpajjanaṃ, tato kammaṭṭhānavisodhanena samathanipphatti, tato samāhitassa āraddhavipassakassa vipassanāpāripūri. Paripuṇṇavipassano maggasammādiṭṭhiṃ paribrūhetīti evametesaṃ aṅgānaṃ paramparāya sammukhā ca anuggaṇhanato ayamānupubbī kathitāti veditabbaṃ.

In five instances, the word 'anta' should be understood as indicating the meaning of cause. For in this way, the analogy of the mango, spoken of with 'just as...' and so on, would also be fitting. 'Udakakoṭṭhaka' refers to a water basin. 'Thiraṃ katvā bandhati' means to fasten firmly, making it neither too loose nor too tight, neither too large nor too small. 'Thiraṃ karoti' means to strengthen the water basin more firmly during irrigation, preventing water from leaking out. 'Sukkha-daṇḍaka' refers to the dry branch tip of that same mango tree. 'Kipillika-puṭa' means a nest of red ants. 'Khaṇitti' refers to a hoe. The binding of the water basin is like virtue, because it is the root of the means for the growth of right view. Watering is like listening to the Dhamma, because it nourishes development. Strengthening the boundary is like serenity, because it brings firmness to the boundary of virtue, which is the foundation for the development mentioned. For one who is composed, virtue becomes even firmer. The removal of nearby creepers and such is like the cutting off of stumbling and slipping in the meditation subject, because it removes hindrances to the desired development. Digging up the roots is like the development of the seven contemplations, because it digs up craving, conceit, and wrong views, which are the roots of that hindrance. And here, because for one of perfectly purified virtue who engages in the meditation subject, listening to suitable Dhamma is desirable; then engaging in discussion on the meaning as heard; then the accomplishment of serenity by purifying the meditation subject; then the completion of insight for one who is composed and has begun insight. One whose insight is complete develops right view of the path. Thus, this gradual teaching should be understood as having been spoken because these factors support each other sequentially and directly.

453. Idha kiṃ pucchatīti idha evaṃ arahattaphalaṃ pāpitāya desanāya “kati panāvuso, bhavā”ti bhavaṃ pucchanto kīdisaṃ anusandhiṃ upādāya pucchatīti attho. Teneva hi “mūlameva gato anusandhī”ti vatvā adhippāyaṃ [M 2.0270] pakāsento “duppañño”tiādimāha. Duppaññoti hi idha appaṭividdhasacco adhippeto, na jaḷo eva. Kāmabhavotiādīsu kammopapattibhedato duvidhopi bhavo adhippetoti dassento “kāmabhavūpagaṃ kamma”ntiādimāha. Tattha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ visuddhimagge taṃsaṃvaṇṇanāyaṃ (visuddhi. 2.647; visuddhi. mahāṭī. 2.646-647) vuttanayena veditabbaṃ. Punabbhavassāti punappunaṃ aparāparaṃ bhavanato jāyanato punabbhavoti laddhanāmassa vaṭṭapabandhassa. Tenāha “idha vaṭṭaṃ pucchissāmī”ti. Abhinibbattīti bhavayonigatiādivasena nibbatti. Tahiṃ tahiṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ bhavādike. Abhinandanāti taṇhāabhinandanahetu. Gamanāgamanaṃ hotītiādinā bhavādīsu sattānaṃ aparāparaṃ cutipaṭisandhiyo dasseti. Khayanirodhenāti accantakhayasaṅkhātena anuppādanirodhena. Ubhayametaṃ na vattabbaṃ pahānābhisamayabhāvanābhisamayānaṃ [V 2.0250] accāsannakālattā. Vattabbaṃ taṃ hetuphaladhammūpacāravasena. Yathā hi padīpujjalanahetuko andhakāravigamo, evaṃ vijjuppādahetuko avijjānirodho, hetuphaladhammā ca samānakālāpi pubbāparakālā viya voharīyanti yathā – “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti (ma. ni. 1.204, 400; ma. ni. 3.420, 425, 426; saṃ. ni. 2.43-45; 2.4.60; kathā. 465, 467) paccayapaccayuppannakiriyā. Gamanaṃ upacchijjati idha kāmabhave parinibbānena. Āgamanaṃ upacchijjati tattha rūpārūpesu parinibbānena. Gamanāgamanaṃ upacchijjati sabbaso aparāparuppattiyā abhāvato.

453. Here, what is being asked? Here, in this discourse that has led to the fruit of arahantship, when asking about existence with the words 'How many existences, friend?', the meaning is: what kind of continuity is being referred to? For this reason, having said 'He has gone to the root of the continuity,' he reveals his intention by saying 'one of little wisdom,' and so on. For here, 'one of little wisdom' is intended to mean one who has not penetrated the truth, not merely a dullard. In the phrases 'existence in the sensual realm,' etc., both types of existence—that which is due to kamma and that which is due to rebirth—are intended, as shown by 'kamma leading to existence in the sensual realm,' and so on. What needs to be said there should be understood according to the method stated in the Visuddhimagga and its commentary (Visuddhi. 2.647; Visuddhi. Mahāṭī. 2.646-647). 'Again-becoming' (punabbhava) refers to the bondage of the cycle (vaṭṭapabandha), which has gained the name 'again-becoming' because of its repeated and successive becoming and arising. Therefore, he said, 'Here, I will ask about the cycle.' 'Rebirth' (abhinibbatti) means arising by way of existence, origin, destination, and so on. 'Here and there' refers to various existences and the like. 'Delight' (abhinandanā) is caused by the delight of craving. By 'coming and going,' etc., he shows the successive deaths and rebirths of beings in various existences. 'By destruction and cessation' refers to the cessation of non-arising, which is called complete destruction. Neither of these should be spoken of, because the time of the realization of abandonment and the realization of development is exceedingly near. It should be spoken of in terms of the conventional usage of cause-and-effect phenomena. Just as the disappearance of darkness is caused by the lighting of a lamp, so the cessation of ignorance is caused by the arising of knowledge. And cause-and-effect phenomena, even though simultaneous, are conventionally spoken of as having a sequence, as in: 'Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises' (M. Ni. 1.204, 400; M. Ni. 3.420, 425, 426; S. Ni. 2.43-45; 2.4.60; Kathā. 465, 467)—the function of conditions and conditioned phenomena. 'Going is cut off' means by final Nibbāna here in the sensual realm. 'Coming is cut off' means by final Nibbāna there in the form and formless realms. 'Coming and going are cut off' means due to the complete absence of successive arising.

454. Vivaṭṭakathāya parato jotitaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ vivaṭṭaṃ patvā ṭhitassa ukkaṭṭhaniddesena ubhatobhāgavimuttassa nirodhasādhakaṃ vibhāvituṃ yuttanti āha “katamaṃ panāvusoti idha kiṃ pucchatī”tiādi. Tathā hi anantaraṃ nirodhasamāpajjanakena bhikkhunā jānitabbāni paṭhamassa jhānassa sampayogapahānaṅgāni pucchitāni. Aṅgavavatthānanti jhānaṅgavavatthānaṃ. Koṭṭhāsaparicchedoti tattha labbhamānaphassapañcamakādidhammakoṭṭhāsaparicchedo jānitabbo. Imasmiṃ jhāne ettakā dhammā saṃvijjanti, ettakā nirodhitāti jānitabbaṃ. Upakārānupakārāni aṅgānīti nirodhasamāpattiyā upakārāni ca anupakārāni ca aṅgāni. Nirodhasamāpattiyā hi soḷasahi ñāṇacariyāhi navahi samādhicariyāhi ca pattabbattā taṃtaṃñāṇassa samādhicariyāhi samatikkamitabbā dhammā anupakārakaṅgāni, samatikkamakā [M 2.0271] upakārakaṅgāni. Tesañhi vasena yathānupubbaṃ upasantupasantaoḷārikabhāvāya bhavaggasamāpattiyā saṅkhārāvasesasukhumataṃ pattā cittacetasikā yathāparicchinnaṃ kālaṃ nirujjhanti, appavattiṃ gacchanti. Tassāti nirodhassa. Anantarapaccayanti anantarapaccayasadisaṃ. Na hi nirodhassa koci dhammo anantarapaccayo nāma atthi. Yañhi tadā cittacetasikānaṃ tathā nirujjhanaṃ, taṃ yathāvuttapubbābhisaṅkhārahetukāya nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā ahosīti sā tassa anantarapaccayo viya hotīti taṃ vuttaṃ. Cha samāpattiyoti suttantanayena vuttasuttantapiṭakasaṃvaṇṇanāti katvā. “Satta samāpattiyo”ti pana vattabbaṃ, aññathā idaṃ “caturaṅgika”nti na vattabbaṃ siyā. Nayaṃ vā dassetvāti ādiantadassanavasena nayadassanaṃ katvā.

454. After the discourse on emergence, it is appropriate to clarify that which accomplishes cessation for one liberated in both ways, who has attained and is established in the first jhāna, which was clarified as emergence, by means of a superior description. Thus, he said, 'But what, venerable sirs? Here, what is being asked?' and so on. For immediately after, the factors of association and abandonment of the first jhāna, which should be known by the bhikkhu who is about to enter cessation, are questioned. 'Determination of factors' refers to the determination of jhāna factors. 'Delineation of sections' means that the delineation of the sections of phenomena—the group of five with contact as the fifth and so on—that are found there should be known. In this jhāna, it should be known how many phenomena are present and how many have ceased. 'Helpful and unhelpful factors' refers to the factors that are helpful and unhelpful for the attainment of cessation. For the attainment of cessation is to be reached through sixteen modes of knowledge and nine modes of concentration; therefore, the phenomena to be transcended by the modes of concentration of each respective knowledge are the unhelpful factors, while those that facilitate transcendence are the helpful factors. By their means, consciousness and mental factors, having gradually become more and more tranquil from grosser states and having reached the extreme subtlety of the remainder of formations through the attainment of the peak of existence, cease for a predetermined period and become inactive. 'Of that' means of cessation. 'An immediate condition' means like an immediate condition. For there is no phenomenon whatsoever that is an immediate condition for cessation. For the cessation of consciousness and mental factors at that time in that way occurred because of the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, which was caused by previous volitional formations as stated before; thus, it is like an immediate condition for it, so it was said. 'Six attainments' is said because it is an exposition of the Suttanta Piṭaka stated according to the Suttanta method. However, it should be said, 'seven attainments,' otherwise this could not be called 'fourfold.' 'Or having shown the method' means having demonstrated the method by showing the beginning and the end.

455. Evaṃ nirodhassa pādakaṃ vibhāvetvā idāni antonirodhe anupabandhabhāvato pañcannaṃ pasādānaṃ paccayapucchane paṭhamaṃ tāva te sarūpato āveṇikato āveṇikavisayato paṭissaraṇato ca pucchanavasena pāḷi pavattāti dassento “viññāṇanissaye pañca pasāde pucchanto”ti [V 2.0251] āha. Gocaravisayanti ettha kāmaṃ tabbahulacāritāpekkhaṃ gocaraggahaṇaṃ, anaññatthabhāvāpekkhaṃ visayaggahaṇanti attheva gocaravisayabhāvānaṃ viseso, vivariyamānaṃ pana ubhayampi ārammaṇasabhāvamevāti āha “gocarabhūtaṃ visaya”nti. Ekekassāti eko ekassa, añño aññassāti attho. Aññattho hi ayaṃ eka-saddo “ittheke abhivadantī”tiādīsu (ma. ni. 3.27) viya. Sace hītiādi abhūtaparikappanavacanametaṃ. Tattha samodhānetvāti ekajjhaṃ katvā. Vināpi mukhenātiādinā atthasallāpikanidassanaṃ nāma dasseti. Yathā viññāṇādhiṭṭhitameva cakkhu rūpaṃ passati, na kevalaṃ, evaṃ cakkhunissayameva viññāṇaṃ taṃ passati, na itaranti āha “cakkhupasāde upanehī”ti. Tena tesaṃ tattha saṃhaccakāritaṃ dasseti. Yadi vā nīlaṃ yadi vā pītakanti idaṃ nīlapītādisabhāvajānanamattaṃ sandhāyāha. Nīlaṃ pītakanti pajānanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa nattheva avikappakabhāvato. Etesaṃ cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ. Nissayasīsena nissitapucchā hesā, evañhi visayānubhavanacodanā samatthitā hoti. Tenāha “cakkhuviññāṇaṃ hī”tiādi. Yathāsakaṃ visayaṃ rajjanādivasena anubhavituṃ [M 2.0272] asamatthāni cakkhuviññāṇādīni, tattha samatthatāyeva ca natthi, na kiñci atthato paṭisarantāni viya hontīti vuttaṃ “kiṃ etāni paṭisarantī”ti. Javanamano paṭisaraṇanti pañcadvārikaṃ itarañca sādhāraṇato vatvā puna yāya’ssa rajjanādipavattiyā paṭisaraṇatā, sā savisesā yattha labbhati, taṃ dassento “manodvārikajavanamano vā”ti āha. Etasmiṃ pana dvāreti cakkhudvāre javanaṃ rajjati vā dussati vā muyhati vā, yato tattha aññāṇādiasaṃvaro pavattati.

455. Having thus clarified the basis of cessation, now, due to the state of non-binding in internal cessation, to show that the Pāli text proceeds by way of questioning the conditions of the five sense faculties—firstly in terms of their own nature, their uniqueness, their unique domain, and their reliance—he said, 'When questioning about the five sense faculties dependent on consciousness.' Here, regarding 'domain and object,' although the grasping of the domain is with respect to frequent activity therein, and the grasping of the object is with respect to its not being elsewhere, there is indeed a distinction between the state of being a domain and an object. However, when explained, both are essentially of the nature of an object; hence he says, 'the object that is the domain.' 'Of each one' means one for one, another for another. For this word 'eka' has another meaning, as in 'some here declare' (MN 22) and so on. 'If so,' and so on, is a statement of unreal supposition. Here, 'having combined' means having brought them together. By 'even without the mouth,' and so on, he shows an example of meaningful conversation. Just as the eye sees form only when supported by consciousness, not by itself, so too consciousness sees it only when supported by the eye faculty, not otherwise; thus he says, 'bring it near to the eye faculty.' Thereby, he shows their acting in concert in that regard. 'Whether blue or yellow' is said referring merely to the knowing of the nature of blue, yellow, and so on. The knowing 'it is blue,' 'it is yellow' does not belong to eye-consciousness, because it is non-conceptual. 'Of these' means of eye-consciousness and so on. This is a question about the dependent under the heading of the support, for in this way the prompting to experience the object is established. Hence he says, 'for eye-consciousness,' and so on. Eye-consciousness and the like are incapable of experiencing their respective objects by way of lusting and so on; there is no such capability in them at all. They are as if not relying on anything in reality; thus it is said, 'What do these rely on?' 'The impulsional mind is the reliance'—having said this generally of the five-door process and the other, he then shows where that reliance, which is the activity of lusting and so on, is found with its specifics, stating, 'or the impulsional mind of the mind-door.' In this door, that is, in the eye-door, the impulsion lusts, or hates, or is deluded, because non-restraint due to ignorance and so on occurs there.

Tatrāti tasmiṃ javanamanasseva paṭisaraṇabhāve. Dubbalabhojakāti hīnasāmatthiyā rājabhoggā. Sevakānaṃ gaṇanāya yojitadivase labbhamānakahāpaṇo yuttikahāpaṇo. Andubandhanena baddhassa vissajjanena labbhamānakahāpaṇo bandhakahāpaṇo. Kiñci paharante mā paharantūti paṭikkhipato dātabbadaṇḍo māpahārakahāpaṇo. So sabbopi parittakesu gāmikamanussesu tathā labbhamāno ettako hotīti āha “aṭṭhakahāpaṇo vā”tiādi. Satavatthukanti satakarīsavatthukaṃ. Esa nayo sesapadadvayepi. Tatthātiādi upamāsaṃsandhanaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyameva.

'In that' means in that state of reliance of the impulsional mind itself. 'Those who eat the weak' means royal stipends for those of inferior capacity. The 'proper kahāpaṇa' is the kahāpaṇa obtained on the day appointed for the reckoning of servants. The 'bond kahāpaṇa' is the kahāpaṇa obtained by releasing one bound with a fetter. The 'do-not-strike kahāpaṇa' is the fine to be paid by one who objects, saying 'Do not strike!' to someone who is striking. He said, 'eight kahāpaṇas or,' and so on, indicating that all of this, when obtained in that manner from minor village folk, amounts to so much. 'Having a basis of a hundred' means having a property of one hundred karīsas. This method applies to the remaining two phrases as well. 'In that,' and so on, is the connection with the simile; that is easily understood.

456. Antonirodhasmiṃ pañca pasādeti nirodhasamāpannassa pavattamāne pañca pasāde. Kiriyamayapavattasminti javanādikiriyānibbattakadhammappavattiyaṃ. Balavapaccayā hontīti pacchājātavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayehi paccayā honti, upatthambhakabhāvena balavapaccayā honti. Jīvitindriyaṃ paṭiccāti indriyaatthiavigatapaccayavasena paccayabhūtaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ paṭicca [V 2.0252] pañcavidhopi pasādo tiṭṭhati. Jīvitindriyena vinā na tiṭṭhati jīvitindriyarahitassa kammasamuṭṭhānarūpakalāpassa abhāvato. Tasmāti yasmā anupālanalakkhaṇena jīvitena anupālitā eva usmā pavattati, na tena ananupālitā, tasmā usmā āyuṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati. Jālasikhaṃ paṭicca ābhā paññāyatīti jālasikhāsaṅkhātabhūtasaṅghātaṃ saheva pavattamānaṃ nissāya “ābhā”ti laddhanāmā vaṇṇadhātu “ujjalati, andhakāraṃ vidhamati, rūpagatāni ca vidaṃsetī”tiādīhi pakārehi ñāyati. Taṃ ālokaṃ paṭiccāti taṃ vuttappakāraṃ ālokaṃ paccayaṃ labhitvā. Jālasikhā paññāyatīti “appikā, mahatī, uju, kuṭilā”tiādinā pākaṭā hoti.

456. 'In internal cessation, the five sense faculties' means the five sense faculties that are occurring for one who has attained cessation. 'In the occurrence produced by the functional' means in the occurrence of phenomena produced by functional consciousness such as impulsion. 'They are strong conditions' means they are conditions by way of postnascence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance conditions; they are strong conditions because they are supportive. 'Dependent on the life faculty' means the fivefold sense faculty persists dependent on the life faculty, which is a condition by way of faculty, presence, and non-disappearance. It does not persist without the life faculty, because there is no material group originated by kamma that is devoid of the life faculty. 'Therefore' means: since heat persists only when sustained by life, which has the characteristic of sustaining, and not when unsustained by it, therefore heat persists dependent on life. 'Light is perceived dependent on the flame' means: the color element, which has received the name 'light,' depending on the aggregate of primary elements called the flame with which it occurs simultaneously, is known by such modes as 'it shines, dispels darkness, and reveals forms.' 'Dependent on that light' means having obtained that light of the aforesaid kind as a condition. 'The flame is perceived' means it becomes manifest as 'small, large, straight, crooked,' and so on.

Jālasikhā [M 2.0273] viya kammajatejo nissayabhāvato. Āloko viya jīvitindriyaṃ tannissitabhāvato. Idāni upamopamitabbānaṃ sambandhaṃ dassetuṃ “jālasikhā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ālokaṃ gahetvāva uppajjatīti iminā yathā jālasikhāya saheva āloko uppajjati, evaṃ kammajusmanā saheva jīvitindriyaṃ uppajjatīti dasseti. Jālasikhāsannissayo tassā satiyeva honto āloko tāya uppādito viya hotīti āha “attanā janitaālokenevā”ti. Usmā nāmettha kammasamuṭṭhānā tejodhātu tannissitañca jīvitindriyaṃ tadanupālakañcāti āha “kammajamahābhūtasambhavena jīvitindriyena usmāya anupālana”nti. Na kevalaṃ khaṇaṭṭhitiyā eva, atha kho pabandhānupacchedassapi jīvitindriyaṃ kāraṇanti āha “vassasatampi kammajatejapavattaṃ pāletī”ti. Usmā āyuno paccayo honto sesabhūtasahito eva hotīti āha “mahābhūtānī”ti. Tathā āyupi sahajātarūpaṃ pālentameva usmāya paccayo hotīti vuttaṃ “mahābhūtāni pāletī”ti.

Like the flame of a lamp, the heat produced by karma exists due to its dependence. Like light, the life faculty exists due to its dependence on that. Now, to show the connection between the simile and the thing to be compared, it is said: 'For the flame...' By stating, 'it arises only accompanied by light,' it shows that just as light arises together with the flame, so too the life faculty arises together with the heat produced by karma. The dependence on the flame is such that when it exists, light appears as if produced by it—thus it is said: 'by the light generated by itself.' Here, 'heat' refers to the karma-produced fire element, the life faculty that is dependent on it, and that which sustains it—thus it is said: 'the sustaining of heat by the life faculty, which arises from the great elements produced by karma.' Not only for a momentary existence, but the life faculty is also the cause of uninterrupted continuity—thus it is said: 'It protects the continuation of heat produced by karma even for a hundred years.' Heat, being a condition for life-span, exists together with the remaining elements—thus it is said: 'the great elements.' Similarly, life-span, while sustaining the co-nascent form, is also a condition for heat—thus it is said: 'it sustains the great elements.'

457. Āyu eva indriyapaccayādivasena sahajātadhammānaṃ anupālanavasena saṅkharaṇato āyusaṅkhāro. Bahuvacananiddeso pana anekasatasahassabhedesu rūpakalāpesu pavattiyā anekabhedanti katvā. Ārammaṇarasaṃ anubhavantīti vedaniyā yathā “niyyānikā”ti. Tenāha “vedanā dhammāvā”ti. Sukhādibhedabhinnattā bahuvacananiddeso. Imesaṃ āyusaṅkhāravedanānaṃ ekantanirodhaṃ samāpannassa maraṇena bhavitabbaṃ vedanāya niruddhattā. Āyusaṅkhārānaṃ tathā aniruddhattā nirodhassa samāpajjanameva na siyā, kuto vuṭṭhānaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ pāḷiyaṃ “te ca hāvuso”tiādi. Vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyati saññāvedanādīnaṃ uppattiyā. Idāni tamatthaṃ vitthārato upamāya vibhāvetuṃ “yo hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ukkaṇṭhitvāti nānārammaṇāpātato nibbinditvā. Yathāparicchinnakālavasenāti yathāparicchinne kāle sampatte. Rūpajīvitindriyapaccayāti indriyapaccayabhūtā[V 2.0253]. Jālāpavattaṃ viya arūpadhammā tejussadabhāvato visayobhāsanato ca. Udakappahāro viya nirodhasamāpattiyā pubbābhisaṅkhāro. Pihitaaṅgārā viya rūpajīvitindriyaṃ usmāmattatāya anobhāsanato[M 2.0274]. Yathāparicchinnakālāgamananti yathāparicchinnakālassa upagamanaṃ. Anurūpapattivaseneva rūpapavattiggahaṇaṃ. Imaṃ rūpakāyaṃ jahantīti imasmā rūpakāyā kaḷevarā vigacchanti nappavattanti.

457. Life itself is the life-formation because it forms by way of maintaining co-nascent states through conditions such as the faculty condition. The explanation in the plural is given because its occurrence in many hundreds of thousands of different material groups makes it of many kinds. They are called 'to be felt' because they experience the taste of the object, as in the phrase 'leading out.' Therefore, it is said, 'or are feelings phenomena?' The explanation in the plural is given because they are divided into types such as pleasure, etc. For one who has attained the complete cessation of these life-formations and feelings, death must occur because feeling has ceased. Since the life-formations have not ceased in the same way, not even the attainment of cessation would be possible—how much less emergence from it? Hence, it is said in the Pāli, 'And those, friends,' etc. Emergence is known through the arising of perception, feelings, etc. Now, to explain that meaning in detail by means of a simile, it is said, 'For one who,' etc. 'Having become discontented' means having become disenchanted due to the impact of various objects. 'By way of the predetermined time' means when the predetermined time has arrived. 'The condition which is the material life faculty' means it has become the faculty condition. Like the continuation of a flame, immaterial phenomena are so due to their fiery nature and the illumination of objects. Like a stroke of water, the prior formation for the attainment of cessation. Like covered embers, the material life faculty is mere heat and does not illuminate. 'The arrival of the predetermined time' means the approach of the predetermined time. The grasping of the continuity of form occurs simply by way of a suitable rebirth-linking. 'They abandon this material body' means they depart from this material body, this corpse, and do not continue.

Kāyena saṅkharīyantīti kāyasaṅkhārā tappaṭibaddhavuttitāya. Vācaṃ saṅkharontīti vacīsaṅkhārā. Vitakketvā vicāretvā hi vācaṃ bhindati katheti. Cittena saṅkharīyantīti cittasaṅkhārā tappaṭibaddhavuttito. Cittasaṅkhāranirodhacodanāya rūpanirodho viya cittanirodho acodito tesaṃ tato aññattāti na cittasampayuttanirodho ekantiko vitakkādinirodhe tadabhāvato. Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ “vācā aniruddhā hotī”ti, tampi na. Vācaṃ saṅkharontīti hi vacīsaṅkhārā, tesu niruddhesu kathaṃ vācāya anirodho. Cittaṃ pana niruddhesupi cittasaṅkhāresu tehi anabhisaṅkhatattā vitakkādinirodho viya pavattatiyevāti ayamettha parassa adhippāyo. Ānantariyakammaṃ kataṃ bhaveyya, cittassa aniruddhattā taṃ nissāya ca rūpadhammānaṃ anapagatattā te jīvanti eva nāmāti. Byañjane abhinivesaṃ akatvāti “cittasaṅkhārā niruddhā”ti vacanato teva niruddhā, na cittanti evaṃ neyyatthaṃ suttaṃ “nītattha”nti abhinivesaṃ akatvā. Ācariyānaṃ naye ṭhatvāti paramparāgatānaṃ ācariyānaṃ adhippāye ṭhatvāti attho. Upaparikkhitabboti suttantarāgamato suttantarapadassa aviparīto attho vīmaṃsitabbo. Yathā hi “asaññabhavo”ti vacanato “saññāva tattha natthi, itare pana cittacetasikā santī”ti ayamettha attho na gayhati. Yathā ca “nevasaññānāsaññāyatana”nti vacanato “saññāva tattha tādisī, na phassādayo”ti ayamettha attho na gayhati saññāsīsena desanāti katvā, evamidhāpi “cittasaṅkhārā niruddhā”ti, “saññāvedayitanirodho”ti ca desanāsīsameva. Sabbepi pana cittacetasikā tattha nirujjhantevāti ayamettha aviparīto attho veditabbo, tathāpubbābhisaṅkhārena sabbesaṃyeva cittacetasikānaṃ tattha nirujjhanato. Etena yaṃ pubbe “aññattā, tadabhāvato”ti ca yuttivacanaṃ, tadayuttaṃ adhippāyānavabodhatoti dassitaṃ hoti. Tenāha “attho hi paṭisaraṇaṃ, na byañjana”nti.

Bodily formations are so called because they are formed by the body, due to their connection with it. Verbal formations are so called because they form speech; for one thinks and reflects before one breaks into speech. Mental formations are so called because they are formed by the mind, due to their connection with it. The prompting for the cessation of mental formations does not prompt the cessation of mind, just as it does not prompt the cessation of form, because they are different. Therefore, the cessation of mind-concomitants is not absolute with the cessation of thought and examination, because of the absence of that. However, what was said—'speech is not ceased'—that too is not so. For verbal formations are what form speech, so how could speech not cease when they have ceased? But the mind, even when mental formations have ceased, continues to exist, not being formed by them, just as with the cessation of thought and so on. This is the opinion of others here. An act with immediate result could be done; because the mind has not ceased and because material phenomena dependent on it have not departed, they are indeed alive. 'Without insisting on the phrasing' means not taking the statement 'mental formations are ceased' to mean that only they are ceased and not the mind, and thus not insisting on understanding a sutta with implicit meaning as having explicit meaning. 'Standing by the tradition of the teachers' means adhering to the intention of the teachers handed down through generations. 'It should be examined' means the correct meaning of a sutta passage should be investigated in accordance with other suttas. For just as from the statement 'the non-percipient realm,' one does not take the meaning that perception alone is absent there while other mental factors remain; and just as from the statement 'the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,' one does not take the meaning that perception alone is of that kind while contact and other factors are not, because the teaching is given with perception as the heading; so too here, the statements 'mental formations are ceased' and 'the cessation of perception and feeling' are merely the heading of the teaching. Yet all mental factors whatsoever cease there—this is the correct meaning to be understood, because all mental and associated phenomena cease there through the prior volitional formations. By this it is shown that the previous reasoned statement—'because of difference, due to their absence'—is inappropriate due to a lack of understanding the intended meaning. Therefore, it is said: 'The meaning is the refuge, not the phrasing.'

Upahatānīti [M 2.0275] bādhitāni. Makkhitānīti dhaṃsitāni. Ārammaṇaghaṭṭanāya indriyānaṃ kilamatho cakkhunā bhāsurarūpasukhumarajadassanena vibhāvetabbo. Tathā hi uṇhakāle purato aggimhi [V 2.0254] jalante kharassare ca paṇave ākoṭite akkhīni bhedāni viya na sahanti sotāni “sikharena viya abhihaññantī”ti vattāro honti.

'Upahatāni' means afflicted. 'Makkhitāni' means defiled. The fatigue of the faculties due to the impact of objects should be illustrated by the eye's seeing of bright forms and subtle dust. For instance, in hot weather, when a fire is blazing in front and a harsh-sounding drum is beaten, the eyes cannot endure it, as if they are being split, and of the ears it is said, 'they are struck as if by a peak.'

458. Rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānameva rūpavirāgabhāvanāvasena pavattaṃ arūpajjhānanti nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ vissajjento dhammasenāpati “sukhassa ca pahānā”tiādinā vissajjesi. Apagamanena vigamena paccayā apagamanapaccayā sukhādippahānāni. Adhigamapaccayā pana kasiṇesu rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānaṃ heṭṭhimā tayo ca āruppā. Na hi sakkā tāni anadhigantvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanamadhigantuṃ. Nirodhato vuṭṭhānakaphalasamāpattinti nirodhato vuṭṭhānabhūtaṃ aniccānupassanāsamudāgataphalasamāpattiṃ. Sā hi “animittā cetovimuttī”ti vuccati. Yathā samathanissando abhiññā, mettākaruṇāmuditābrahmavihāranissando upekkhābrahmavihāro, kasiṇanissando āruppā, samathavipassanānissando nirodhasamāpatti, evaṃ vipassanāya nissandaphalabhūtaṃ sāmaññaphalanti āha “vipassanānissandāya phalasamāpattiyā”ti. Ārammaṇā nāma sārammaṇadhammānaṃ visesato uppattinimittanti āha “sabbanimittānanti rūpādīnaṃ sabbārammaṇāna”nti. Natthi ettha kiñci saṅkhāranimittanti animittā, asaṅkhatā dhātūti āha “sabbanimittāpagatāya nibbānadhātuyā”ti. Phalasamāpattisahajātaṃ manasikāraṃ sandhāyāha, na āvajjanamanasikāraṃ. Na hettha tassa sambhavo anulomānantaraṃ uppajjanato.

458. The fourth jhāna of the form sphere, when it proceeds by way of cultivating dispassion for form, is a formless jhāna. The General of the Dhamma, in explaining the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, did so with the words, "by the abandoning of pleasure," and so forth. The abandonments of pleasure, etc., are conditions for departure by means of departing and ceasing. But the conditions for attainment are the fourth jhāna of the form sphere in the kasiṇas and the three lower formless attainments. For it is impossible to attain the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception without first attaining those. 'Fruition-attainment of emerging from cessation' means the fruition-attainment that has arisen from the contemplation of impermanence, which is the emergence from cessation. This is called 'the signless liberation of mind.' Just as supernormal knowledge is the outflow of serenity, the divine abiding of equanimity is the outflow of the divine abidings of loving-kindness, compassion, and altruistic joy, the formless attainments are the outflow of the kasiṇas, and the attainment of cessation is the outflow of serenity and insight, so he speaks of the fruit of recluseship, which is the resultant fruit that is the outflow of insight, with the words 'by the fruition-attainment which is the outflow of insight.' 'Objects' are specifically the cause for the arising of phenomena that have objects; therefore, he said, 'of all signs,' meaning 'of all objects such as form,' and so forth. 'There is no conditioned sign here,' thus it is signless; 'it is the unconditioned element,' thus he said, 'of the Nibbāna-element, which is devoid of all signs.' He refers to the attention that arises together with the fruition-attainment, not to the attention of adverting. For in this case, there is no possibility of that, since it arises immediately after conformity.

Imasmiṃ ṭhāneti idha vuttanirodhassa ādimajjhapariyosānānaṃ gahitānaṃ imasmiṃ pariyosānassa gahitaṭṭhāne. Dvīhi balehīti samathavipassanābalehi. Tayo ca saṅkhārānanti kāyasaṅkhārādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ. Soḷasahi ñāṇacariyāhīti aniccānupassanā, dukkhā, anattā, nibbidā, virāgā, nirodhā, paṭinissaggā, vivaṭṭānupassanā, sotāpattimaggo…pe… arahattaphalasamāpattīti imāhi soḷasahi ñāṇacariyāhi. Navahi samādhicariyāhīti paṭhamajjhānasamādhiādīhi navahi samādhicariyāhi. Yo [M 2.0276] yathāvuttāsu cariyāsu puggalassa vasībhāvo, sā vasībhāvatāpaññā. Assā sā kathitāti yojanā. Vinicchayakathāti vinicchayavasena pavattā aṭṭhakathā kathitā. Tasmā visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 2.868-869) taṃsaṃvaṇṇanāyañca (visuddhi. mahāṭī. 2.868) vuttanayena veditabbā.

'In this place' means in this context where the beginning, middle, and end of the cessation spoken of here have been grasped, specifically at this point where the end is grasped. 'By two powers' means by the powers of serenity and insight. 'And the three formations' means the three formations, beginning with the bodily formation. 'By sixteen modes of knowledge-conduct' means by these sixteen modes of knowledge-conduct: contemplation of impermanence, suffering, non-self, disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, relinquishment, contemplation of turning away, the path of stream-entry... up to... the attainment of the fruition of arahantship. 'By nine modes of concentration-conduct' means by these nine modes of concentration-conduct, beginning with the concentration of the first jhāna. The mastery a person has over the modes of conduct described, that is the wisdom of mastery. The connection is that it is spoken of as belonging to this. 'The exposition of discrimination' means the commentary that proceeds by way of discrimination is spoken. Therefore, it should be understood according to the method stated in the Visuddhimagga (Vism. XXIII, 28-29) and in its commentary (Vism-mhṭ. II, 868).

Valañjanasamāpatti ariyavihāravasena viharaṇasamāpatti. Ṭhitiyāti ettha pabandhaṭṭhiti adhippetā, na khaṇaṭṭhiti. Kasmā? Samāpajjanattā. Tenāha “ṭhitiyāti ciraṭṭhitattha”nti. Addhānaparicchedoti [V 2.0255] ettakaṃ kālaṃ samāpattiyā vītināmessāmīti pageva kālaparicchedo. Rūpādinimittavasenāti kammakammanimittagatinimittesu yathārahaṃ labbhamānarūpādinimittavasena. Tattha yasmā kammanimitte chabbidhampi ārammaṇaṃ labbhati, tasmā “sabbanimittāna”nti vuttaṃ, na sabbesaṃ ārammaṇānaṃ ekajjhaṃ, ekantato vā manasikātabbato. Lakkhaṇavacanañhetaṃ yathā “dātabbametaṃ bhesajjaṃ, yadi me byādhitā siyu”nti.

The attainment of common use is the attainment of dwelling by means of the noble abiding. Here, 'standing' refers to continuous standing, not momentary standing. Why? Because of entering into attainment. Therefore, he said, ''standing' means lasting for a long duration.' 'Delimiting the period' means determining beforehand how much time will be spent in the attainment—indeed, it is the delimitation of time. 'By means of the signs of form, etc.' refers to the signs of form, etc., obtained appropriately among the kamma, the sign of kamma, and the sign of destiny. Here, since all six kinds of objects are obtained in the sign of kamma, it is said 'of all signs,' not meaning that all objects are to be attended to simultaneously or exclusively. For this is a statement of characteristic, just as it is said: 'This medicine should be given, if I were to become ill.'

459. Nīlampi sañjānātītiādinā nīlādiggahaṇamukhena taṃvaṇṇānaṃ sattānaṃ sañjānanaṃ averādibhāvamanasikaraṇaṃ jotitanti āha “etasmiñhi ṭhāne appamāṇā cetovimutti kathitā”ti. Ettha ākiñcaññaṃ kathitanti sambandho. “Ettha suññatā”ti, “ettha animittā”ti etthāpi eseva nayo. Nti “idha aññaṃ abhinavaṃ nāma natthī”tiādinā vuttaṃ atthavacanaṃ. Etāti appamāṇacetovimuttiādayo. Ekanāmakāti ekekanāmakā, ye nānābyañjanāti adhippetā. Eko dhammoti arahattaphalasamāpatti. Catunāmakoti appamāṇacetovimuttiādināmako. Etanti etamatthaṃ. Appamāṇāti anodhiso, odhisopi vā “ettakā”ti aparimitā. Asesetvāti asubhasamāpatti viya ekasseva aggahaṇato.

459. By the phrase 'perceives blue,' etc., through the means of grasping blue and other hues, the perception of beings of that color and the attention to the state of non-enmity, etc., is illuminated. Thus, he said, 'For in this case, the immeasurable liberation of mind is spoken of.' Here, the connection is: 'Nothingness is spoken of.' Similarly, for 'Here is emptiness,' and 'Here is the signless,' this same method applies. The 'ṃ' refers to the meaning stated in the phrase 'Here, there is nothing else new whatsoever,' etc. 'These' means the immeasurable liberation of mind and the others. 'Having one name' means each has a single name, which are intended as 'having different expressions.' 'One Dhamma' is the fruition-attainment of Arahantship. 'Having four names' means being named 'immeasurable liberation of mind,' etc. 'This' refers to this meaning. 'Immeasurable' means without a boundary, or even with a boundary, it is unlimited as 'so much.' 'Without remainder' means because of not grasping only one aspect, like the attainment of foulness.

Kiñcāpi asubhanimittārammaṇampi kiñcanaṃ hoti, ārammaṇasaṅghaṭṭanassa kiñcanassa asubhasamāpattīnampi paṭibhāganimittasaṅkhātaṃ ārammaṇaṃ sabimbaṃ viya viggahaṃ kiñcanaṃ hutvā upaṭṭhāti, na tathā imassāti. Nanu brahmavihārapaṭhamāruppānampi paṭibhāganimittabhūtaṃ kiñci ārammaṇaṃ natthīti? Saccaṃ natthi, ayaṃ pana paṭhamāruppaviññāṇaṃ viya na paṭibhāganimittabhūtaārammaṇatāya evaṃ vuttā. Attenāti [M 2.0277] attanā. Bhavati etena attāti abhidhānaṃ buddhi cāti bhāvo, attā. Bhāva-saddopi attapariyāyoti āha “bhāvaposapuggalādisaṅkhātenā”ti. Nesaṃ appamāṇasamādhiādīnaṃ catunnaṃ. “Nānatā pākaṭāvā”ti vuttaṃ nānattaṃ bhūmito ārammaṇato ca dassetuṃ “attho panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Parittādibhāvena atītādibhāvena ajjhattādibhāvena ca na vattabbaṃ ārammaṇaṃ etissāti navattabbārammaṇā nibbānārammaṇaphalasamāpattibhāvato.

Although the object that is the sign of foulness is a 'something' (a hindrance), and for the attainments of foulness the object called the counterpart sign appears as a 'something'—a body like a clear image—due to the impingement of the object, it is not so in this case. Now then, for the divine abodes and the first formless attainment, is there not some object that is a counterpart sign? Indeed, there is not. However, this is not spoken of thus because of having an object that is a counterpart sign, unlike the consciousness of the first formless attainment. 'By self' means by oneself. 'One exists by this, thus it is self (attā); the designation and understanding is being (bhāva), self (attā).' The word 'bhāva' (being) is also a synonym for 'attā' (self); therefore, he said 'by what is designated as being, nourisher, individual, and so forth.' For these four—the immeasurable concentrations and so on—to show the diversity from the plane and from the object, which was stated as 'the diversity is evident,' the words 'the meaning, moreover,' and so on, were stated. Its object should not be described in terms of being limited, etc., past, etc., or internal, etc.; therefore, it has an indescribable object, because of being the fruition attainment which has Nibbāna as its object.

Ettakoti rāgādīhi saṃkiliṭṭhatāya ettakappamāṇo, uttāno parittacetasoti attho. Nibbānampi appamāṇameva pamāṇakaraṇānaṃ abhāvenāti ānetvā sambandho. Akuppāti arahattaphalacetovimutti paṭipakkhehi akopanīyatāya. Kiñcatīti kattari paṭhito dhātu maddanatthoti [V 2.0256] āha “kiñcati maddatī”ti. Tassa payogaṃ dassetuṃ “manussā kirā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

'Ettako' (of such extent) means of such a measure due to being defiled by lust and so on; the meaning is shallow, of limited mind. Nibbāna, too, is immeasurable due to the absence of means of measuring—thus the connection is drawn. 'Unshakable' means the liberation of mind that is the fruit of arahantship, because it is unshakeable by opposing factors. 'Kiñcati'—the root is cited in the active voice and means to crush; hence he said, 'kiñcati means it crushes.' To illustrate its usage, it is stated, 'People, indeed...' and so on.

Samūhādighanavasena sakiccaparicchedatāya ca saviggahā viya upaṭṭhitā saṅkhārā niccādiggāhassa vatthutāya “niccanimittaṃ sukhādinimitta”nti ca vuccati. Vipassanā pana tattha ghanavinibbhogaṃ karontī niccādiggāhaṃ vidhamentī “nimittaṃ samugghātetī”ti vuttā ghananimittassa ārammaṇabhūtassa abhāvā. Na gahitāti ekatthapadaniddese pāḷiyaṃ kasmā na gahitā? Sāti suññatā cetovimutti. Sabbatthāti appamāṇācetovimuttiādiniddesesu. Ārammaṇavasenāti ārammaṇavasenapi ekatthā, na kevalaṃ sabhāvasarasatova. Iminā pariyāyenāti appamāṇatotiādinā ārammaṇato laddhapariyāyena. Aññasmiṃ pana ṭhāneti ākiñcaññādisaddapavattihetuto aññena hetunā appamāṇātisaddappavattiyaṃ etassa cetovimuttiyā honti. Esa nayo sesesupi. Iminā pariyāyenāti iminā tāya tāya samaññāya voharitabbatāpariyāyena. Saccānaṃ dassanamukhena vaṭṭavasena uṭṭhitadesanaṃ arahattena kūṭaṃ gaṇhanto yathānusandhināva desanaṃ niṭṭhapesi. Yaṃ panettha atthato avibhattaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyameva.

By way of the massiveness of aggregates and the delineation of their respective functions, the formations appear as if solid, providing a basis for grasping permanence, etc.; hence they are called "the sign of permanence, the sign of pleasure," etc. But insight, by breaking up that solidity and dispelling the grasping of permanence, etc., is said to "uproot the sign," because of the absence of the solid sign which has become its object. "Not grasped"—why is it not taken up in the single-meaning exposition in the Pāli? That is the liberation of mind through emptiness. "In all respects"—this refers to the expositions on the immeasurable liberation of mind, etc. "By way of object"—even by way of object, they are of a single meaning, not merely by their own nature and essence. "By this method" means by the method obtained from the object, such as immeasurability, etc. "But in another case" means that the term "immeasurable" occurs in relation to this liberation of mind for a reason other than the cause for the occurrence of terms like "nothingness," etc. This same method applies to the rest. "By this method" means by this method of how it should be expressed with that particular designation. Through the gateway of seeing the truths, taking the teaching that arose in relation to the cycle of existence to its peak with arahantship, he concluded the teaching in accordance with its sequence. As for what is not explicitly divided here in meaning, it is indeed easily understood.

Mahāvedallasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Exposition of the Hidden Meanings in the Commentary on the Mahāvedalla Sutta is complete.

4. Cūḷavedallasuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Cūḷavedalla Sutta

460. Ayaṃ [M 2.0278][V 2.0257] desanā yasmā pucchāvissajjanavasena pavattā, tasmā pucchakavissajjake pucchānimittañca samudāyato vibhāvetuṃ “ko panāya”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Upāsakattanti amaggāgataṃ upāsakattaṃ. Tesanti ekādasanahutānaṃ. Maggāgatena upasamena santindriyo santamānaso.

460. Since this discourse proceeds by way of questions and answers, therefore, in order to clarify the questioner, the respondent, and the basis of the question as a whole, it is said, “But who is this?” and so on. “The state of a lay follower” refers to the state of a lay follower who has not entered the path. “Of them” refers to the eleven myriads. With the peace attained through the path, with calmed faculties, with a serene mind.

“Kiṃ nu kho ajja bhavissati ayyaputto”ti vīthiṃ olokayamānā. Olambanatthanti tassa hatthāvalambanatthaṃ pubbāciṇṇavasena attano hatthaṃ pasāresi. Bahiddhāti attanā aññaṃ visabhāgavatthuṃ sandhāya vadati. Paribhedakenāti pesuññavādinā.

“What indeed will my lord do today?” she thought, looking down the street. “For support” means for the purpose of taking his hand for support; she extended her hand as she was accustomed to do. “Outside” means she spoke, referring to another, dissimilar thing. “By a divisive person” means by one who speaks slanderously.

Adhigamappicchatāya “na pakāsetabbo”ti cintesi. Puna taṃ anukampanto “sace kho panāha”ntiādiṃ cintesi. Eso dhammoti eso lokuttaradhammo. Vivaṭṭaṃ uddissa upacitaṃ nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ kusalaṃ upanissayo. “Yadi me upanissayo atthi, sakkā etaṃ paṭiladdhuṃ. Sacepi natthi, āyatiṃ upanissayo bhavissatī”ti cirakālaparibhāvitāya ghaṭe padīpajālā viya abbhantare dippamānāya hetusampattiyā codiyamānā āha “evaṃ sante mayhaṃ pabbajjaṃ anujānāthā”ti.

Due to having few wishes regarding his attainment, he thought, “It should not be revealed.” Then, out of compassion for her, he reconsidered, “But if I…” and so on. “This Dhamma” means this supramundane Dhamma. The wholesome qualities conducive to penetration, accumulated aiming at the Unbinding, serve as a supporting condition. “If I have a supporting condition, it is possible to attain this again. Even if I do not have it, in the future a supporting condition will arise” – being urged by this perfection of causes, long-cultivated, blazing within like a lamp flame in a pot, she said, “If this is so, then permit my going forth.”

Lābhasakkāro uppajji sucirakālaṃ katūpacitapuññatāya. Abhinīhārasampannattāti sujātattherassa padumuttarassa bhagavato aggasāvakassa nipaccakāraṃ katvā – “tumhehi diṭṭhadhammassa bhāgī assa”nti nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ dānaṃ datvā katapatthanāsaṅkhātasampannābhinīhārattā. Nāticiraṃ kilamitthāti kammaṭṭhānaṃ bhāventī vipassanāya paripākavasena ciraṃ na kilamittha. Vuttamevatthaṃ vivarituṃ “ito paṭṭhāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Dutiyagamanenāti pabbājanatthaṃ gamanato dutiyagamanena.

Gain and honor arose due to merit made and accumulated over a very long time. Because of being endowed with a perfected aspiration, which means: because of having a perfected aspiration, which is described as the aspiration made after giving a gift conducive to penetration, having paid homage to the Elder Sujāta, the chief disciple of the Blessed One Padumuttara, with the wish, “May I be a sharer of the Dhamma seen by you.” “She did not struggle for very long” means that while developing the meditation subject, she did not struggle for long due to the maturation of insight. To explain this very meaning that was stated, “From this point on,” and so on was stated. “By the second journey” means by the second journey from the journey for the purpose of making her go forth.

Upanetvāti pañhassa atthabhāvena upanetvā. Sakkāyanti sakāyaṃ. Upanikkhittaṃ kiñci vatthuṃ sampaṭicchamānā, viya sampaṭicchantī viya. Eko eva pāso etissāti ekapāsakā, gaṇṭhi. Sā hi sumociyā, anekapāsā pana dummociyā, ekapāsaggahaṇaṃ vissajjanassa sukarabhāvadassanatthaṃ[V 2.0258]. Paṭisambhidāvisaye ṭhatvāti etena theriyā pabhinnapaṭisambhidataṃ dasseti. Paccayabhūtāti ārammaṇādivasena paccayabhūtā.

“Having brought it up” means having brought it up by way of the meaning of the question. “Sakkāya” refers to one’s own body. “Like one accepting some object placed before one” is like accepting, as if accepting. “It has only one noose” thus “ekapāsakā,” a knot. For that is easily untied, but multiple nooses are difficult to untie—the taking up of a single noose is for the purpose of showing the ease of the answer. “Having stood in the domain of the analytical knowledges” indicates the Therī’s state of having attained the analytical knowledges. “Having become a condition” means having become a condition by way of being an object, etc.

Theriyā [M 2.0279] visesādhigamassa attano avisayatāya visākho “na sakkā”tiādinā cintesīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saccavinibbhogapañhabyākaraṇenāti saccapariyāpannassa dhammassa dassanato aññānaññatthaniddhāraṇabhedanāsaṅkhātassa vinibbhogapañhassa vissajjanena. Dve saccānīti dukkhasamudayasaccāni. Paṭinivattetvāti parivattetvā. Gaṇṭhipañhanti dubbinibbedhatāya gaṇṭhibhūtaṃ pañhaṃ.

It should be understood that Visākha, because the Therī’s attainment of distinction was beyond his own domain, thought, “It is not possible,” and so on. “By the explanation of the question concerning the analysis of the truths” means by answering the question on analysis, which is defined as determining and distinguishing the phenomena included in the truths from one another. “Two truths” means the truths of suffering and its origin. “Having turned back” means having turned around. “A knotty question” is a question that is like a knot due to its difficulty in being penetrated.

Na taṃyeva upādānaṃ te pañcupādānakkhandhā ekadesassa samudāyatābhāvato, samudāyassa ca ekadesatābhāvato. Nāpi aññatra pañcahi upādānakkhandhehi upādānaṃ tassa tadekadesabhāvato. Na hi ekadeso samudāyavinimutto hoti. Yadi hi taññevātiādinā ubhayapakkhepi dosaṃ dasseti. Rūpādisabhāvampīti rūpavedanāsaññāviññāṇasabhāvampi, phassacetanādisabhāvampi upādānaṃ siyā. Aññatra siyāti pañcahi upādānakkhandhehi visuṃyeva upādānaṃ yadi siyā. Parasamayeti nikāyavāde. Cittavippayutto anusayoti nidassanamattametaṃ nikāyavāde cittasabhāvābhāvaviññāṇādīnampi cittavippayuttabhāvapaṭijānanato. Evaṃ byākāsīti “na kho, āvuso”tiādinā khandhagatachandarāgabhāvena byākāsi. Atthadhammanicchayasambhavato asambandhena. Tesu katthacipi asammuyhanato avitthāyantena. Pucchāvisaye mohandhakāravigamanena padīpasahassaṃ jālentena viya. Saupādānupādānaṭṭhānaṃ anuttānatāya pacurajanassa gūḷho. Aggahitasaṅketānaṃ kesañci paṭicchāditasadisattā paṭicchanno. Tilakkhaṇabbhāhatadhammavisayatāya tilakkhaṇāhato. Gambhīrañāṇagocaratāya gambhīro. Laddhapatiṭṭhā ariyasaccasampaṭivedhanato. Evaṃ diṭṭhadhammādibhāvato vesārajjappattā. Sabbaso nivutthabrahmacariyatāya tiṇṇaṃ bhavānampi aparabhāge nibbāne nivutthavatīti bhavamatthake ṭhitā.

That very clinging is not the five aggregates of clinging, because a part is not a collection, and a collection is not a part. Nor is clinging apart from the five aggregates of clinging, due to its being a part of them. For a part is not free from the collection. Indeed, by saying “that very,” etc., he points out faults in both positions. The nature of form, etc., too—the nature of form, feeling, perception, and consciousness, or the nature of contact, volition, etc.—could be clinging. If clinging were apart, it would exist separately from the five aggregates of clinging. “In another doctrine” refers to a sectarian view. “A latent tendency dissociated from mind”—this is a mere statement in a sectarian view, because they acknowledge the state of being dissociated from mind even for things like consciousnesses that lack the nature of mind. Thus, she explained—by saying, “No, friend,” etc., she explained it as being the nature of desire and lust for the aggregates. Because of the arising of the determination of meaning and Dhamma without difficulty; because of not being confused about them anywhere, not wavering; by dispelling the darkness of delusion in the domain of the question, it is like lighting a thousand lamps. The state of clinging with its basis is profound for the multitude due to its not being superficial. For some who have not grasped the conventions, it is concealed, being like something covered. It is struck by the three characteristics because its object is phenomena struck by the three characteristics. It is profound because it is the domain of profound knowledge. She has gained a footing through the thorough penetration of the noble truths. Thus, from having seen the Dhamma, etc., she has attained fearlessness. Because the holy life has been lived completely, she stands at the summit of existence, having dwelt in Nibbāna in the latter part of the three existences.

461. “Rūpaṃ attato samanupassatī”ti paduddhāraṃ katvā “idhekacco”tiādinā (paṭi. ma. 1.130) paṭisambhidāpāṭhena tadatthaṃ vivarati. Tattha attato samanupassatīti attāti samanupassati, attabhāvena samanupassati. Ahanti attānaṃ niddisati. Ahaṃbuddhinibandhanañhi attānaṃ attavādī paññapeti, tasmā yaṃ rūpaṃ so ahanti yadetaṃ mama rūpaṃ nāma, so ahanti vuccamāno mama attā [M 2.0280] taṃ mama rūpanti rūpañca attañca advayaṃ anaññaṃ samanupassati. Tathā passato ca attā viya rūpaṃ, rūpaṃ viya vā attā aniccoti āpannameva[V 2.0259]. Accīti jālasikhā. Sā ce vaṇṇo, cakkhuviññeyyāva siyā, na kāyaviññeyyā, vaṇṇopi vā kāyādiviññeyyo acciyā anaññattāti upameyyaṃ viya upamāpi diṭṭhigatikassa ayuttāva. Diṭṭhipassanāyāti micchādiṭṭhisaṅkhātāya passanāya passati, na taṇhāmānapaññānupassanāya. Arūpaṃ vedanādiṃ attāti gahetvā chāyāya rukkhādhīnatāya chāyāvantaṃ rukkhaṃ viya, rūpassa santakabhāvena attādhīnatāya rūpavantaṃ attānaṃ samanupassati. Pupphādhīnatāya pupphasmiṃ gandhaṃ viya ādheyyabhāvena attādhīnatāya rūpassa attani rūpaṃ samanupassati. Yathā karaṇḍo maṇino ādhāro, evaṃ rūpampi attano ādhāroti katvā attānaṃ rūpasmiṃ samanupassati. Eseva nayoti iminā attano vedanādīhi anaññattaṃ tesañcādhāraṇataṃ nissitatañca yathāvuttaṃ atidisati.

461. Having extracted the phrase “He regards form as self,” he explains its meaning with the passage from the Paṭisambhidāmagga beginning with “Here, someone…” (Paṭis I.130). Herein, “he regards form as self” means he regards it as self, he regards it as his own being. “I” refers to the self. For those who hold the doctrine of self, they posit the self based on the notion of ‘I’. Therefore, whatever form there is, he thinks, “This is I,” meaning, “This, which is called my form, is I.” Thus, he regards form and self as non-dual, not other. For one who sees thus, it follows that either the self is like form, or form is like the self—impermanent. “Flame” refers to the crest of a fire. If flame were color, it would be perceptible only to the eye, not to the body. Or, if color were perceptible to the body, etc., it would be due to its non-otherness from the flame. Thus, the simile, like the thing to be compared, is unsuitable for one holding a wrong view. “By seeing with a view” means he sees with the seeing that is called wrong view, not with the contemplation of craving, conceit, or wisdom. Taking the formless (feeling, etc.) as self, he regards the self as possessing form, due to form being its property and dependent on the self, just as a tree possesses shade due to the shade's dependence on the tree. Like the scent in a flower due to its dependence on the flower, so he regards form in the self as something contained, due to form being dependent on the self. Just as a casket is the container of a jewel, so, thinking that form is its container, he regards the self in form. “This is the method”—by this, he extends the aforesaid non-otherness of the self from feeling, etc., and their being a container and being dependent.

Arūpaṃ attāti kathitaṃ “vedanāvanta”ntiādīsu viya rūpena vomissakatāya abhāvato. Rūpārūpamissako attā kathito rūpena saddhiṃ sesārūpadhammānaṃ attāti gahitattā. Ucchedadiṭṭhi kathitā rūpādīnaṃ vināsadassanato. Tenevāha “rūpaṃ attāti yo vadeyya, taṃ na upapajjati, attā me uppajjati ca veti cāti iccassa evamāgataṃ hotī”tiādi. Avasesesūti pannarasasu ṭhānesu. Sassatadiṭṭhi kathitā rūpavantādibhāvena gahitassa aniddhāritarūpattā.

The formless is called self, as in the cases of 'possessing feeling,' etc., because of its not being mixed with form. The self mixed with form and the formless is spoken of because form along with the other formless phenomena are grasped as the self. The annihilation view is spoken of due to seeing the destruction of form, etc. Hence it is said: “If someone were to say, ‘Form is self,’ that is not fitting, for it would follow that ‘my self arises and ceases,’” and so on. In the remaining instances, meaning in the fifteen places. The eternalist view is spoken of because what is grasped as possessing form, etc., is not of a determined form.

Diṭṭhigatiko yaṃ vatthuṃ attāti samanupassati, yebhuyyena taṃ niccaṃ sukhanti ca samanupassateva. Sāvako pana tappaṭikkhepena sabbe dhammā anattāti sudiṭṭhattā rūpaṃ attāti na samanupassati, tathābhūto ca aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti samanupassati, tathā vedanādayoti dassento “na rūpaṃ attato”tiādimāha. Evaṃ bhavadiṭṭhipi avijjābhavataṇhā viya vaṭṭassa samudayoyevāti diṭṭhikathāyaṃ “ettakena gamanaṃ hotī”tiādi. Diṭṭhippahānakathāyañca “ettakena gamanaṃ na hotī”tiādi vuttaṃ.

One who is attached to views regards any object as self, and for the most part perceives it as permanent and pleasurable. However, a disciple, rejecting that, clearly sees all phenomena as not-self, and thus does not regard form as self, and as such perceives form as impermanent, suffering, and not-self. In the same way, showing that feeling and so on are also not self, he says, “Form is not self,” and so on. Thus, even the view of existence, like ignorance, becoming, and craving for existence, is simply the origin of the round. In the discussion on views, it is said, “Progress is made this far,” and in the discussion on abandoning views, it is said, “Progress is not made this far.”

462. Heṭṭhā vuttamatthameva pucchitattā “theriyā paṭipucchitvā vissajjetabbo”ti vatvā paṭipucchanavidhiṃ dassetuṃ “upāsakā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Paṭipattivasenāti [M 2.0281] sakkāyanirodhagāminipaṭipadābhāvena. Saṅkhatāsaṅkhatavasena lokiyalokuttaravasena saṅgahitāsaṅgahitavasenāti “vasenā”ti padaṃ paccekaṃ yojetabbaṃ. Tattha kāmaṃ asaṅkhato nāma maggo natthi, kiṃ saṅkhato, udāhu asaṅkhatoti pana pucchāvasena tathā vuttaṃ? “Ariyo”ti vacaneneva maggassa lokuttarato siddhā, saṅgāhakakhandhapariyāpannānaṃ pana maggadhammānampi siyā lokiyatāti [V 2.0260] idha lokiyaggahaṇaṃ. Kiñcāpi saṅgahitapadameva pāḷiyaṃ āgataṃ, na asaṅgahitapadaṃ, ye pana saṅgāhakabhāvena vuttā, te saṅgahitā na hontīti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ asaṅgahitaggahaṇaṃ katanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saṅkhatotiādīsu samecca sambhuyya paccayehi katoti saṅkhato. Tathābhūto ca taṃsamaṅgino puggalassa pubbabhāgacetanāti mayhaṃ maggo aṭṭhaṅgiko hotu sattaṅgiko vāti cetitabhāvena cetito. Sahajātacetanāyapi cetitova tassā sahakārīkāraṇabhāvato, tato eva pakappito āyūhito. Paccayehi nipphāditattā kato nibbattito ca. Samāpajjantena attano santāne sammadeva āpajjantena uppādentena. Iti sattahipi padehi paccayanibbattitaṃyeva ariyamaggassa dasseti.

462. Since the meaning stated below was questioned, it was said, “One should inquire of the elders and then reply,” and to show the method of inquiry, “lay devotees,” etc., were mentioned. By way of practice—that is, by the nature of the path leading to the cessation of identity. The terms “by way of conditioned and unconditioned,” “by way of mundane and supramundane,” and “by way of included and not included” should each be connected with the word “by way of.” Indeed, there is no path that is unconditioned; but whether it is conditioned or unconditioned is stated in the form of a question. By the word “noble,” the supramundane nature of the path is established, but since the path-elements included in the including aggregates may also be mundane, the term “mundane” is used here. Although only the word “included” appears in the Pāli, not “not included,” the commentary’s inclusion of “not included” should be understood in the sense that those things stated as having the nature of including are not themselves included. In the terms “conditioned,” etc., “conditioned” means made by combining and assembling through causes. And such a path, as the individual’s preliminary volition, is willed by thinking, “May my path be eightfold or sevenfold.” Even the co-nascent volition is willed because it is a cooperating cause for that; hence it is designed and striven for. It is produced by causes and brought about. By one who enters upon it, by rightly undertaking and generating it in one's own continuity. Thus, in all seven terms, it is shown that the noble path is produced by causes.

Asaṅgahito khandhānaṃ padeso etassa atthīti maggo sappadeso. Natthi etesaṃ padesāti khandhā nippadesā. Padissati etena samudāyoti hi padeso, avayavo. Ayanti maggo. Sappadesattā ekadesattā. Nippadesehi samudāyabhāvato niravasesapadesehi. Yathā nagaraṃ rajjekadesabhūtaṃ tadantogadhattā rajjena saṅgahitaṃ, evaṃ ariyamaggo khandhattayekadesabhūto tadantogadhattā tīhi khandhehi saṅgahitoti dasseti “nagaraṃ viya rajjenā”ti iminā. Sajātitoti samānajātitāya, samānasabhāvattā evāti attho. Ettha ca sīlakkhandho “nava koṭisahassānī”tiādinā (visuddhi. 1.20; apa. aṭṭha. 2.55.55; paṭi. ma. aṭṭha. 1.1.37) vuttapabhedavasena ceva sampattasamādānaviratiādivasena ca gayhamāno nippadeso, maggasīlaṃ pana ājīvaṭṭhamakameva samucchedaviratimattamevāti sappadesaṃ. Samādhikkhandho parittamahaggatādivasena ceva upacārappanāsamādhivasena ca anekabhedatāya nippadeso, maggasamādhi pana lokuttarova[M 2.0282], appanāsamādhi evāti sappadeso. Tathā paññākkhandho parittamahaggatādivasena ceva sutamayañāṇādivasena ca anekabhedatāya nippadeso, maggapaññā pana lokuttarāva, bhāvanāmayā evāti sappadesā. Attano dhammatāyāti sahakārīkāraṇaṃ anapekkhitvā attano sabhāvena attano balena appetuṃ na sakkoti vīriyena anupatthambhitaṃ, satiyā ca anupaṭṭhitaṃ. Paggahakiccanti yathā kosajjapakkhe na patitā cittaṭṭhiti, tathā paggaṇhanakiccaṃ. Apilāpanakiccanti yathā ārammaṇe na pilavati, evaṃ apilāpanakiccaṃ.

The path has a portion, because a portion of the aggregates is included in it. The aggregates have no portion, because there is no portion of these. Indeed, a portion is that by which a collection is discerned; it is a constituent. This is the path. Because it has a portion, it has a part. Since the aggregates are without portions, they are entirely without parts. Just as a city, being a part of the kingdom, is included within the kingdom, so too the noble path, being a part of the three aggregates, is included within those three aggregates—this is shown by the phrase, “like a city by a kingdom.” Of the same kind—meaning of similar nature, having the same essence—this is the meaning. Here, the virtue aggregate, described as having “ninety million” divisions and so on, is without portions due to its various classifications, such as attainment, undertaking, and restraint. However, the virtue of the path is only right livelihood as the eighth factor, being solely the restraint of eradication—thus, it has a portion. The concentration aggregate, due to its divisions such as limited and exalted, and due to its many forms like access and absorption, is without portions. But the concentration of the path is solely supramundane, being only absorption—thus, it has a portion. Similarly, the wisdom aggregate, due to its divisions such as limited and exalted, and due to its many forms like knowledge born of learning, is without portions. But the wisdom of the path is solely supramundane, being only born of development—thus, it has a portion. By its own nature—meaning without relying on supporting causes, it cannot apply itself by its own essence or its own strength if not supported by energy and not established by mindfulness. The function of exertion—just as the steadiness of mind does not fall to the side of laziness, so too is the function of exertion. The function of non-wavering—just as it does not waver regarding its object, so too is the function of non-wavering.

Ekato jātāti sahajātā. Piṭṭhiṃ datvā onatasahāyo viya vāyāmo samādhissa ārammaṇe appanāya visesapaccayabhāvato. Aṃsakūṭaṃ datvā ṭhitasahāyo viya sati samādhissa ārammaṇe daḷhapavattiyā paccayabhāvato. Kiriyatoti upakārakiriyato.

“Born together” means “co-nascent.” Like a friend who bends down offering his back, effort serves as a specific condition for the attainment of absorption in the object. Like a friend who stands firm offering his shoulder, mindfulness serves as a condition for the firm persistence on the object of concentration. By way of function means by way of rendering assistance.

Ākoṭetvāti [V 2.0261] ārammaṇaṃ āhanitvā. Tathā hi vitakko “āhananaraso”ti, yogāvacaro ca “kammaṭṭhānaṃ takkāhataṃ vitakkapariyāhataṃ karotī”ti vuccati. Idhāpīti sammādiṭṭhisaṅkappesu. Kiriyatoti vuttappakāraupakārakiriyato.

"Having struck" means having struck the object. For indeed, initial thought is said to have the characteristic of striking, and the yogi is said to "make the meditation subject struck by initial thought, thoroughly assailed by initial thought." "Here too" refers to right view and right intention. "By way of function" means by way of the assisting function of the kind described.

Subhasukhādinimittaggāhavidhamanaṃ catukiccasādhanaṃ. Paccayattenāti sahajātādipaccayabhāvena. Catukiccasādhanavasenevāti idaṃ maggavīriyasseva gahitabhāvadassanaṃ. Tañhi ekaṃyeva hutvā catukiccaṃ yathāvuttaupakārakasabhāvena ca parivāraṭṭhena parikkhāro hoti. Maggasampayuttadhammānanti iminā maggadhammānampi gahaṇaṃ, na taṃsampayuttaphassādīnaṃyeva. Ekacittakkhaṇikāti maggacittuppādavasena ekacittakkhaṇikā.

The dispelling of the grasping of signs such as beauty and happiness is the accomplishment of the fourfold task. "By way of conditionality" means through the nature of conditions such as co-nascence. "By means of accomplishing the fourfold task"—this shows that only path-energy is taken as an example. For that, being one, accomplishes the fourfold task; and by its nature of being helpful as stated and in the sense of being an entourage, it is an accessory. "Of the states associated with the path"—by this, the path-states themselves are also included, not merely contact and other states associated with them. "Lasting for a single mind-moment" means lasting for a single mind-moment by way of the arising of the path-consciousness.

Sattahi ñāṇehīti paramukkaṃsagatehi sattahi javanehi sampayuttañāṇehi, sattahi vā anupassanāñāṇehi. Ādito sevanā āsevanā, tato paraṃ vaḍḍhanā bhāvanā, punappunaṃ karaṇaṃ bahulīkammanti adhippāyenāha “aññena cittenā”tiādi. Adhippāyavasena niddhāretvā gahetabbatthaṃ suttaṃ neyyatthaṃ. Yathārutavasena gahetabbatthaṃ nītatthaṃ. Evaṃ santeti yadi idaṃ suttaṃ nītatthaṃ, āsevanādi ca visuṃ visuṃ cittehi hoti, evaṃ sante. Āsevanādi nāma cittassa anekavāraṃ uppattiyā hoti[M 2.0283], na ekavāramevāti āha “ekaṃ citta”ntiādi. Tatrāyaṃ saṅkhepattho – āsevanāvasena pavattamānaṃ cittaṃ sucirampi kālaṃ āsevanāvaseneva pavatteyya, tathā bhāvanābahulīkammavasena pavattamānānipi, na cettha ettakāneva cittāni āsevanāvasena pavattanti, ettakāni bhāvanāvasena, bahulīkammavasenāti niyamo labbhati. Iti anekacittakkhaṇikaariyamaggaṃ vadantassa dunnivāriyovāyaṃ doso. Yathā pana pubbabhāgepi nānācittesu pavattapariññādikiccānaṃ sammādiṭṭhiādīnaṃ paṭivedhakāle yathārahaṃ catukiccasādhanaṃ, ekacittakkhaṇikā ca pavatti, evaṃ vipassanāya pavattābhisaṅkhāravasena āsevanābhāvanābahulīkammāni paṭivedhakāle ekacittakkhaṇikāneva hontīti vadantānaṃ ācariyānaṃ na koci doso āsevanādīhi kātabbakiccassa tadā ekacittakkhaṇeyeva sijjhanato. Tenāha “ekacittakkhaṇikāvā”tiādi. Sace sañjānātīti sace saññattiṃ gacchati. Yāguṃ pivāhīti uyyojetabbo dhammasākacchāya abhabbabhāvatoti adhippāyo.

"By seven knowledges" means by the seven knowledges associated with the seven supreme impulsion-moments, or by the seven knowledges of insight. "Repetition" (āsevanā) is practice from the beginning; thereafter, "development" (bhāvanā) is growth; "making it abundant" (bahulīkamma) is repeated doing—with this intention it is said, "with another mind," and so on. A sutta whose meaning must be inferred by way of the intention is interpretable (neyyattha). A sutta whose meaning is to be taken as it is stated is definitive (nītattha). "This being the case" means: if this sutta is definitive, and repetition and so on occur with separate minds, this being the case. Repetition and so on occur through the arising of the mind many times, not just once—hence it is said, "one mind," and so on. Here is the summary meaning: a mind proceeding by way of repetition might continue for a very long time just by way of repetition; likewise for those proceeding by way of development and making abundant. And there is no rule found here that so many minds proceed by way of repetition, so many by way of development, and so many by way of making abundant. Thus, for one who says the noble path is of many mind-moments, this fault is difficult to avoid. However, just as in the preliminary stage, right view and so on, which have the functions of full understanding and so on that occur in various minds, accomplish the fourfold task appropriately at the time of penetration, and their occurrence is of a single mind-moment, so too, for the teachers who say that repetition, development, and making abundant—by way of the formations that occurred during insight—are of a single mind-moment at the time of penetration, there is no fault, because the task to be done by repetition and so on is accomplished then in that single mind-moment. Therefore, it is said, "or of a single mind-moment," and so on. "If one perceives" means if one comes to an understanding.
