Vādaṃ patiṭṭhapesīti evaṃ mayā sabbañca vuttaṃ, ananubhūtañca vuttaṃ, tattha yaṃ tayā adhippāyaṃ ajānantena sahasā appaṭisaṅkhāya dosaggahaṇaṃ, taṃ micchāti brahmānaṃ niggaṇhanto bhagavā attano vādaṃ patiṭṭhapesi.

Bhūtāni means produced by conditions. Asambhūtaṃ means not produced by conditions, that is, Nibbāna. Because of the complete absence of causes for the state of non-radiance, it shines everywhere—thus, it is called 'sabbatopabhaṃ'. Therefore, it is said: 'from Nibbāna, indeed,' and so on. As it is stated: 'There, darkness does not exist.' (Netti. 104) Pabhūtameva means existing in a manifest and excellent state. Because it is formless and cannot be indicated, it arises and exists everywhere—thus, it is called 'sabbatopabhaṃ'. Therefore, it is said: 'from the eastern direction, etc.' Pavisanti ettha means 'they enter here,' which becomes pavisaṃ. By changing the letter 'sa' to 'bha' and eliding 'vi,' it is said as 'pabha'. Therefore, it is said: 'the name of the ford'. Vādaṃ patiṭṭhapesi means: 'Thus, I have stated everything, including what has not been experienced. Therein, your fault-finding, done hastily and without reflection by you who do not understand my intention, is wrong.' Thus, the Blessed One, rebuking the Brahmā, established his own doctrine.

Gahitagahitanti “idaṃ nicca”ntiādinā gahitagahitaṃ gāhaṃ. Tattha tattha dosadassanamukhena niggaṇhantena satthārā vissajjāpito kiñci gahetabbaṃ attano paṭisaraṇaṃ adisvā parājayaṃ paṭicchādetuṃ laḷitakaṃ kātukāmo vādaṃ pahāya iddhiyā pāṭihāriyalīḷaṃ dassetukāmo. Yadi sakkosi mayhaṃ antaradhāyituṃ, na pana sakkhissasīti adhippāyo. Mūlapaṭisandhiṃ gantukāmoti attano pākatikena attabhāvena ṭhātukāmo. So hi paṭisandhikāle nibbattasadisatāya mūlapaṭisandhīti vutto. Aññesanti heṭṭhā aññakāyikānaṃ brahmūnaṃ. Na adāsi abhisaṅkhatakāyenevāyaṃ tiṭṭhatu, na pākatikarūpenāti cittaṃ uppādesi. Tena so abhisaṅkhatakāyaṃ apanetuṃ avisahanto attabhāvapaṭicchādakaṃ andhakāraṃ nimminituṃ ārabhi. Satthā taṃ tamaṃ viddhaṃseti. Tena vuttaṃ “mūlapaṭisandhiṃ vā”tiādi.

Gahitagahitaṃ means the grasping of what is grasped, as in 'this is permanent,' and so on. Dismissed by the Teacher, who rebuked him by pointing out faults in various ways, and not seeing any refuge for himself, he sought to conceal his defeat. Desiring to perform a playful feat, he abandoned the debate and wished to display a miraculous feat of supernormal power. His intention was: 'Let me disappear from you if I can; but you, however, will not be able to.' Desiring to return to the root rebirth means he wished to remain in his natural state. For at the moment of rebirth-linking, due to the similarity of what has arisen, it is called the root rebirth. Aññesaṃ refers to the Brahmās of other realms below. He did not allow it, forming the intention: 'Let him remain in this artificially created body, and not in his natural form.' Therefore, being unable to remove the artificial body, he began to create darkness to conceal his own form. The Teacher dispelled that darkness. Hence it is said: 'or the root rebirth,' and so on.

Bhavevāhanti bhave eva ahaṃ. Ayañca eva-saddo aṭṭhānapayuttoti dassento āha “ahaṃ bhave bhayaṃ disvāyevā”ti, sabbasmiṃ bhave jātiādibhayaṃ ñāṇacakkhunā yāthāvato disvā. Sattabhavanti sattasaṅkhātaṃ bhavaṃ. Kammabhavapaccaye hi upapattibhave sattasamaññā. Vibhavanti vimuttiṃ. Pariyesamānampi upāyassa anadhigatattā bhaveyeva disvā. Bhavañca vibhavesinaṃ vibhavaṃ nibbutiṃ esamānānaṃ sattānaṃ bhavaṃ, bhavesu uppattiñca disvāti evaṃ vā ettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Na abhivadinti “aho vata sukha”nti evaṃ abhivadāpanākārābhāvato na abhinivisiṃ, lakkhaṇavacanametaṃ. Gāhattho eva vā abhivāda-saddoti āha “nābhivadi”nti, “na [M 2.0319] gavesi”nti. Bhavaggahaṇenettha dukkhasaccaṃ, nandīgahaṇena samudayasaccaṃ, vibhavaggahaṇena nirodhasaccaṃ, nandiñca na upādiyinti iminā maggasaccaṃ pakāsitanti āha “iti cattāri saccāni pakāsento”ti. Tadidaṃ catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ gāthāya vibhāvanadassanaṃ. Satthā pana tesaṃ brahmūnaṃ ajjhāsayānurūpaṃ saccāni vitthārato pakāsento vipassanaṃ pāpetvā arahattena desanāya kūṭaṃ gaṇhi. Te ca brahmāno keci sotāpattiphale, keci sakadāgāmiphale, keci anāgāmiphale, keci arahatte ca patiṭṭhahiṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ “saccāni pakāsento satthā dhammaṃ desesī”tiādi. Acchariyajātāti sañjātacchariyā. Samūlaṃ bhavanti taṇhāvijjāhi samūlaṃ bhavaṃ.

Bhavevāhaṃ means 'in existence, indeed, I.' And showing that this word 'eva' is used in the wrong place, it is said: 'It is precisely because I have seen fear in existence,' meaning, having truly seen with the eye of wisdom the fear of birth and so on in all existence. Sattabhavaṃ means existence designated as a 'being'. For in the existence of rebirth conditioned by kamma-existence, the designation 'being' arises. Vibhavaṃ means liberation. Even while seeking, due to not having found the means, only existence is seen. Or, the meaning here should be understood thus: seeing existence, and for beings seeking non-existence—that is, for beings seeking non-existence, Nibbāna—seeing their existence and their arising in existences. Na abhivadiṃ means I did not acclaim, as in 'Ah, indeed, happiness!' Thus, because there was no occasion for acclaiming, I did not cling; this is a statement of a characteristic. Or, the word 'abhivāda' itself means grasping—hence it is said: 'I did not acclaim,' meaning 'I did not seek'. Here, by the mention of existence, the truth of suffering is shown; by the mention of delight, the truth of origin; by the mention of non-existence, the truth of cessation; and by 'and I did not cling to delight,' the truth of the path is revealed. Thus it is said: 'revealing the four truths.' This is the exposition of the four noble truths through the verse. The Teacher, however, in accordance with the inclinations of those Brahmās, extensively revealed the truths, led them to insight, and brought the teaching to its climax with arahantship. And of those Brahmās, some were established in the fruit of stream-entry, some in the fruit of once-returning, some in the fruit of non-returning, and some in arahantship. Therefore it is said: 'revealing the truths, the Teacher taught the Dhamma,' and so on. Acchariyajātā means those in whom wonder had arisen. Samūlaṃ bhavaṃ means existence with its root, rooted in craving and ignorance.

505. Mama [V 2.0297] vasaṃ ativattitānīti sabbaso kāmadhātusamatikkamanapaṭipadāya mayhaṃ visayaṃ atikkamitāni. Kathaṃ panāyaṃ tesaṃ ariyabhūmisamokkamanaṃ jānātīti? Nayaggāhato – “samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ desento saṃsāre ādīnavaṃ, nibbāne ca ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsento veneyyajanaṃ nibbānaṃ diṭṭhameva karoti, tassa desanā avañjhā amoghā indena vissaṭṭhavajirasadisā, tassa ca āṇāya ṭhitā saṃsāre na dissantevā”ti nayaggāhena anumānena jānāti. Sace tvaṃ evaṃ anubuddhoti yathā tvaṃ paresaṃ saccābhisambodhaṃ vadati, evaṃ tvaṃ attano anurūpato sayambhuñāṇena buddho dhammaṃ paṭivijjhitvā ṭhito. Taṃ dhammaṃ mā upanayasīti tayā paṭividdhadhammaṃ mā sāvakapaṭivedhaṃ pāpesi. Idanti idaṃ anantaraṃ vuttaṃ brahmaloke patiṭṭhānaṃyeva sandhāya māro vadati, te dassento “anuppanne hī”tiādimāha. Apāyapatiṭṭhānaṃ pana ājīvakanigaṇṭhādipabbajjaṃ upagate titthakare, ye keci vā pabbajitvā micchāpaṭipanne jane sandhāya vadati. Anuppanneti asañjāte, appatteti attho. Anullapanatāyāti yathā māro upari kiñci uttaraṃ lapituṃ na sakkoti, evaṃ tathā uttarabhāsanena. Nimantanavacanenāti viññāpanavacanena. Brahmaṃ seṭṭhaṃ nimantanaṃ, brahmuno vā nimantanaṃ ettha atthīti brahmanimantanikaṃ, suttaṃ. Yaṃ panettha atthato avibhattaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyameva.

505. Mama vasaṃ ativattitāni means: they have completely transcended my domain through the practice leading to the overcoming of the sensual realm. How then does he know of their entry into the noble stage? He knows by inference through grasping the method: 'The ascetic Gotama, while teaching the Dhamma, reveals the dangers in saṃsāra and the benefits in Nibbāna, making Nibbāna directly visible to those capable of being trained. His teaching is fruitful, not in vain, like a thunderbolt hurled by Indra. And those who abide by his command are no longer seen in saṃsāra.' Thus, he knows by inference through grasping the method. Sace tvaṃ evaṃ anubuddho means: 'If you have awakened thus'—just as you declare the realization of truth by others—'then you stand having penetrated the Dhamma with your own self-originated knowledge, in accordance with your nature.' Taṃ dhammaṃ mā upanayasi means: 'Do not lead that Dhamma on'—that is, do not cause the Dhamma you have penetrated to be realized by mere disciples. Idaṃ: Māra says this referring to what was just said about establishment in the Brahmā world, showing them by saying, 'For those not yet born,' and so on. But as for establishment in the plane of misery, he says this referring to the heretical teachers who have gone forth as Ājīvakas, Nigaṇṭhas, and so on, or to any people who have gone forth but follow a wrong path. Anuppanne means not arisen, that is, not attained. Anullapanatāya means by a further speech such that Māra is unable to utter anything more in reply. Nimantanavacanena means by words of invitation or information. Brahmanimantanikaṃ, the sutta, is so called because it contains a holy, supreme invitation, or because there is an invitation of a Brahmā in it. Whatever meaning here is not analyzed should be easily understood.

Brahmanimantanikasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The explanation of the hidden meaning in the commentary on the Brahmanimantanika Sutta is complete.

10. Māratajjanīyasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Discourse on the Rebuke of Māra

506. Koṭṭhamanupaviṭṭhoti [M 2.0320][V 2.0298] āsayo vaccaguttaṭṭhānatāya koṭṭhaṃ, tassa abbhantarañhettha koṭṭhaṃ. Anurūpo hutvā paviṭṭho anupaviṭṭho. Sukhumañhi tadanucchavikaṃ attabhāvaṃ māpetvā ayaṃ tattha paviṭṭho. Garugaro viyāti garukagaruko viya. U-kārassa hi o-kāraṃ katvā ayaṃ niddeso, ativiya garuko maññeti attho. Garugaru viya icceva vā pāṭho. Māsabhattaṃ māso uttarapadalopena, māsabhattena ācitaṃ pūritaṃ māsācitaṃ maññe. Tenāha “māsabhattaṃ bhuttassa kucchi viyā”ti. Uttarapadalopena vinā atthaṃ dassetuṃ “māsapūritapasibbako viyā”ti vuttaṃ. Tintamāso viyāti tintamāso pasibbako viya. Kiṃ nu kho etaṃ mama kucchiyaṃ pubbaṃ bhārikattaṃ, kiṃ nu kho kathaṃ nu kho jātanti adhippāyo? Upāyenāti pathena ñāyena. Byatirekato panassa anupāyaṃ dassetuṃ “sace panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Attānameva vā sandhāya “mā tathāgataṃ vihesesī”ti āha. Yathā hi ariyasaṅgho “tathāgataṃ devamanussapūjitaṃ, saṅghaṃ namassāma suvatthi hotū”tiādīsu (khu. pā. 6.18; su. ni. 241) tathāgatoti vuccati, evaṃ tappariyāpannā ariyapuggalā, yathā ca purimakā dutiyaaggasāvakā kappānaṃ satasahassādhikaṃ ekaṃ asaṅkhyeyyaṃ pāramiyo pūretvā āgatā, ayampi mahāthero tathā āgatoti tathāgatoti. Patiaggaḷeva aṭṭhāsīti aggaḷassa bahibhāge aṭṭhāsi.

506. "Having entered the koṭṭha": here, 'koṭṭha' refers to the abdomen, as it is a place for storing excrement; and here, 'koṭṭha' means its inner part. "Anupaviṭṭho" means he entered suitably. For having fashioned a subtle body suitable for that, he entered there. "Like a garugaro" means as if very heavy. This explanation is given by changing the 'u' vowel to 'o'; the meaning is, 'it seems extremely heavy.' Alternatively, the reading could be "like a garugaru." It seems `māsācitaṃ`, that is, filled with a month's meal; here `māsa` is by elision of the latter part of `māsabhattaṃ`. Hence it is said, "like the belly of one who has eaten a month's meal." To show the meaning without elision of the latter part, it is said, "like a sack filled with beans." "Like a tintamāsa" means like a sack of wet beans. "What is this previous heaviness in my belly? How has it come about?" — this is the intent. "By means" means by a path, by a method. But to show the absence of means by way of contrast, it is said, "but if," and so on. Or referring to himself, he said, "do not harass the Tathāgata." Just as the noble Sangha is called 'Tathāgata' in phrases like "the Tathāgata, honored by gods and humans, we pay homage to the Sangha, may there be well-being," so too are the noble individuals included in that; and just as the second chief disciples of the past, having fulfilled the perfections over one hundred thousand aeons and one incalculable aeon, came, this great elder has likewise come, hence 'Tathāgata.' "Stood right at the bolt" means he stood outside the bolt.

507. Rukkhadevatā nāma cātumahārājikesu nihīno kāyo, tasmā nesaṃ manussagandho paricitattā nātijegucchoti āha “ākāsaṭṭhadevatāna”nti. Ābādhaṃ karotīti dukkhaṃ janeti. Nāgarikoti sukumāro. Paricokkhoti sabbaso sucirūpo. Ñātikoṭinti ñātibhāgaṃ. Anādimati hi saṃsāre ñātibhāgarahito nāma satto kassacipi natthīti adhippāyo. Idanti “so me tvaṃ bhāgineyyo hosī”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ. Paveṇivasenāti tadā mayhaṃ bhāgineyyo hutvā idāni māraṭṭhāne ṭhitoti imissā paveṇiyā vasena vuttaṃ. Aññassa vā vesamaṃ dhuro vidhuro. Tenāha “aññehi saddhiṃ asadiso”ti. Appadukkhenāti sukheneva. Panthānaṃ [M 2.0321] avanti gacchantīti pathāvino. Ettakenāti ettāvatā citakasannisayena. Udakaleṇanti udakanissandanaleṇaṃ. Samāpattitoti nirodhasamāpattito. Samāpattiphalanti nirodhasamāpattiphalaṃ.

507. "Tree deities" are an inferior class among the devas of the Four Great Kings; therefore, for them, the scent of humans is not very repulsive because they are familiar with it. Thus it is said, "for sky-dwelling deities." "Causes affliction" means it produces suffering. "Citified" means delicate. "Utterly purified" means of completely pure form. "Kin-group portion" means the portion of relatives. For in beginningless saṃsāra, there is no being whatsoever who is devoid of a portion of relatives — this is the meaning. "This" means this statement: "so you were my nephew." "By way of lineage" means: it is said by way of this lineage that "having been my nephew then, he now stands in the position of Māra." Or, `vidhuro` means one without an unequal yoke. Hence it is said, "unlike others." "With little suffering" means with ease alone. "Those who go protecting the path are travelers (`pathāvino`)." "By this much" means by this proximity to the funeral pyre. "Water-cave" means a cave from which water drips. "From attainment" means from the attainment of cessation. "Fruit of attainment" means the fruit of the attainment of cessation.

508. Dasahi akkosavatthūhīti dasahipi akkosavatthūhi, tato kiñci ahāpentā. Paribhāsathāti [V 2.0299] garahatha. Ghaṭṭethāti anūnāhi kathāhi imesu ovijjhatha. Dukkhāpethāti citte dukkhaṃ janetha. Etesanti tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tumhākaṃ akkosanādīhi bhikkhūnaṃ kilesuppattiyā. Tenettha dūsī māro otāraṃ labhati nāmāti adhippāyo. Upaṭṭhātabbaṃ ibhaṃ arahantīti ibbhā, hatthibhaṇḍakā, hīnajīvikatāya hete ibbhā viyāti ibbhā, te pana sadutiyakavasena “gahapatikā”ti vuttā. Kaṇhāti kaṇhābhijātikā. Pādato jātattā pādānaṃ apaccā. Ālasiyajātāti kasivaṇijjādikammassa akaraṇena sañjātālasiyā. Gūthaniddhamanapanāḷīti vaccakūpato gūthassa nikkhamapadeso.

508. "By the ten grounds for abuse" means by all ten grounds for abuse, without omitting anything. "Paribhāsatha" means to censure. "Ghaṭṭetha" means to assail them with unabridged words. "Dukkhāpetha" means to generate suffering in their minds. "Etesan": for the arising of defilements in those monks through your abuse and so on. The meaning is that in this way the defiling Māra finds an opportunity. "Ibbhā": those who are worthy of having an elephant to attend on them; they are elephant-traders. Or, because of their low livelihood, they are like servants. But when with a companion, they are called 'householders.' "Kaṇhā" means of dark lineage. Because they are born from the feet, they are the descendants of the feet. "Ālasiyajātā" means those in whom laziness has arisen from not doing work like agriculture and trade. "Gūthaniddhamanapanāḷī" means the channel for the removal of excrement, the place of exit for excrement from a latrine pit.

Manussānaṃ akusalaṃ na bhaveyya tesaṃ tādisāya abhisandhiyā abhāvato. Āvesakassa ānubhāvena āviṭṭhassa cittasantati viparivattatīti vuttovāyamattho. Visabhāgavatthunti bhikkhūnaṃ santike itthirūpaṃ, bhikkhunīnaṃ santike purisarūpanti īdisaṃ, aññaṃ vā pabbajitānaṃ asāruppaṃ visabhāgavatthuṃ. Vippaṭisārārammaṇanti passantānaṃ vippaṭisārassa paccayaṃ. Lepayaṭṭhinti lepalittaṃ vākurayaṭṭhiṃ.

For humans, unwholesomeness would not arise, since they lack such an intention. Through the power of the possessing spirit, the mental continuity of the possessed person is transformed – this is the meaning stated. "Visabhāgavatthu" means an unsuitable object, such as a female form in the presence of monks, or a male form in the presence of nuns, or any other object unsuitable for renunciants. "Vippaṭisārārammaṇa" means a condition for remorse in those who see it. "Lepayaṭṭhi" means a fowler's stick smeared with bird-lime.

510. Somanassavasenāti gehassitasomanassavasena. Aññathattanti uppilāvitattaṃ. Purimanayenevāti “sace māro manussānaṃ sarīre adhimuccitvā”tiādinā pubbe vuttanayena. Yadi mārova tathā kareyya, manussānaṃ kusalaṃ na bhaveyya, mārasseva bhaveyya, sarīre pana anadhimuccitvā tādisaṃ pasādanīyaṃ pasādavatthuṃ dassesi. Tenāha “yathā hī”tiādi.

510. "Somanassavasena" means through joy associated with household life. "Aññathatta" means being elated. "By the previous method" means by the method previously stated, beginning with "If Māra, having taken possession of human bodies..." If Māra were to act in that way, wholesomeness would not belong to the humans, it would belong to Māra alone; but without taking possession of their bodies, he showed such a pleasing object that inspires confidence. Hence it is said, "For as..." and so on.

511. Asubhasaññāparicitenāti sakalaṃ kāyaṃ asubhanti pavattāya saññāya sahagatajjhānaṃ asubhasaññā, tena paricitena paribhāvitena. Cetasā [M 2.0322] cittena. Bahulanti abhiṇhaṃ. Viharatoti viharantassa, asubhasamāpattibahulassāti attho. Patilīyatīti saṅkucati tattha paṭikūlatāya saṇṭhitattā. Patikuṭatīti apasakkati. Pativattatīti nivattati. Tato eva na sampasāriyati. Rasataṇhāyāti madhurādirasavisayāya taṇhāya.

511. "Asubhasaññāparicitena": 'asubhasaññā' is the jhāna accompanied by the perception that occurs as 'the entire body is foul'; 'paricitena' means practiced, cultivated by that. "Cetasā": with the mind. "Bahulaṃ" means frequently. "Of one who dwells (`viharato`)": the meaning is, of one who frequently abides in the attainment of foulness. "Patilīyati" means it shrinks back, because it is established there with repulsiveness. "Patikuṭati" means it recoils. "Pativattati" means it turns back. For that very reason, it does not spread out. "Rasataṇhāya" means by craving for tastes such as sweet and so on.

Sabbaloke anabhiratisaññāti tīsupi bhavesu aruccanavasena pavattā vipassanābhāvanā. Nibbidānupassanā hesā. Lokacitresūti hatthiassarathapāsādakūṭāgārādibhedesu ceva ārāmarāmaṇeyyakādibhedesu ca loke cittavicittesu. Rāgasantāni vūpasantarāgāni. Dosamohasantānīti etthāpi eseva nayo. Imesaṃ evaṃ kammaṭṭhānaggahaṇaṃ sabbesaṃ sappāyabhāvato.

"Perception of non-delight in the whole world" is the development of insight that occurs through displeasure towards the three existences. This is the contemplation of revulsion. "In the world's varied scenes" means in the diverse and variegated things in the world, with their varieties such as elephants, horses, chariots, palaces, and gabled mansions, as well as parks, pleasant groves, and so on. "Rāgasantāni" means those whose lust is calmed. "Dosamohasantāni": here too, the same method applies. The taking up of these meditation subjects in this way is because they are suitable for all.

512. Sakkharaṃ [V 2.0300] gahetvāti sakkharāsīsena tattakaṃ bhinnapāsāṇamuṭṭhinti āha “antomuṭṭhiyaṃ tiṭṭhanapamāṇaṃ pāsāṇa”nti. Muṭṭhipariyāpannanti attho. Ayañhi pāsāṇassa heṭṭhimakoṭi. Hatthināgoti mahāhatthī. Mahantapariyāyo nāga-saddoti keci. Ahināgādito vā visesanatthaṃ hatthināgoti vuttaṃ. Sakalasarīreneva nivattitvā apalokesīti vuttamatthaṃ vivarituṃ “yathā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Na vāyanti ettha vā-saddo avadhāraṇatthoti āha “neva pamāṇaṃ aññāsī”ti. Sahāpalokanāyāti ca vacanatoti iminā vacanena imaṃ vacanamattaṃ gahetvāti adhippāyo. Uḷāreti uḷāraguṇe. Bhagavantañhi ṭhapetvā natthi tadā sadevake loke tādiso guṇavisesayuttoti.

512. "Taking a piece of gravel": this means a handful of broken stone, as much as a heap of gravel. It is said, "a stone of a size that can be held within the fist." The meaning is that it is contained within the fist. This is indeed the lower limit for a stone. "Hatthināga" means a great elephant. Some say the word "nāga" is a synonym for 'great.' Or, to distinguish it from serpent-nāgas and so on, it is called "hatthināga." To explain the stated meaning, "having turned with its entire body, it looked," it is said, "Just as..." and so on. In "Na vāyanti," the word 'vā' is used for emphasis, as stated: "it did not know the measure at all." And regarding the phrase "sahāpalokanāya," the intention is that this phrase is to be taken literally. "Uḷāre" refers to exalted qualities. For at that time, apart from the Blessed One, there was no one in the world with its gods who possessed such distinguished qualities.

Visuṃ visuṃ paccattavedaniyo ayasūlena saddhiṃ bhūtāni cha phassāyatanāni etassāti cha phassāyatanaṃ, dukkhaṃ. Taṃ ettha atthīti cha phassāyataniko, nirayo. Tenāha “chasu phassā…pe… paccayo”ti. Samāhanatīti samāhato, anekasatabhedo saṅkusamāhato ettha atthīti saṅkusamāhato, nirayo. Visesapaccayatāya vedanāya ṭhitoti vedaniyo, kāraṇākārakena vinā paccattaṃ sayameva vedaniyoti paccattavedaniyo. Ayasūlena saddhiṃ ayasūlanti pādapadesato paṭṭhāya nirantaraṃ abhihananavasena āgatena paṇṇāsāya [M 2.0323] janehi gahitena ayasūlena saha sīsapadesato paṭṭhāya āgataṃ. Ayasūlabhāvasāmaññena cetaṃ ekavacanaṃ, satamattāni patitāni sūlāni. Iminā te ṭhānena cintetvāti nissitavohārena nissayaṃ vadati. Evaṃ vuttanti “tadā jāneyyāsi vassasahassaṃ me niraye paccamānassā”ti evaṃ vuttaṃ. Vuṭṭhānimanti vuṭṭhāne bhavaṃ, antimanti attho. Tenāha “vipākavuṭṭhānavedana”nti, vipākassa pariyosānaṃ vedananti attho. Dukkhatarā hoti padīpassa vijjhāyanakkhaṇe mahantabhāvo viya.

Visuṃ visuṃ paccattavedaniyo: to be experienced individually, by each one. Cha phassāyatanaṃ: the six sense bases are beings along with iron spikes; this belongs to it, thus it is the six sense bases, which are suffering. Cha phassāyataniko: that suffering is present here, thus it is a hell. Therefore, it is said: 'In the six contacts... the condition.' Samāhanatīti samāhato: 'samāhanati' means struck together. Saṅkusamāhato: here there is striking by many hundreds of barbs, thus it is a hell. Vedaniyo: established in feeling by way of a special condition. Paccattavedaniyo: to be experienced individually by oneself, without a doer or an agent. Ayasūlena saddhiṃ: along with an iron spike. Ayasūla refers to an iron spike that has come continuously from the soles of the feet upwards, wielded by fifty men, along with one that has come from the head downwards. This is a singular term due to the common characteristic of being an iron spike, even though hundreds of spikes have fallen. Having considered their position in this way, it speaks of the support by way of dependent designation. Evaṃ vuttaṃ: thus it is said, 'Then you would know, for a thousand years I have been burning in hell.' Vuṭṭhānimanti: 'vuṭṭhāne bhavaṃ' means occurring at the emergence; the meaning is 'at the end.' Therefore, it is said: 'vipākavuṭṭhānavedana,' meaning the feeling at the cessation of the result. It is more painful, like the great intensity at the moment a lamp is extinguished.

513. Ghaṭṭayitvā pothetvā. Pāṭiyekkavedanājanakāti paccekaṃ mahādukkhasamuppādakā. Ayato apagato nirayo, so devadūtasuttena (ma. ni. 3.261) dīpetabbo. Atthavaṇṇanā panassa parato sayameva āgamissati. Imaṃ pana atītavatthuṃ āharitvā attano ñāṇānubhāvadīpanamukhena māraṃ santajjento mahāthero “yo etamabhijānātī”ti gāthamāha. Tassattho – yo mahābhiñño etaṃ kammaṃ kammaphalañca hatthatale ṭhapitaṃ āmalakaṃ viya abhimukhaṃ katvā paccakkhato jānāti. Sabbaso bhinnakilesatāya bhikkhu sammāsambuddhassa aggasāvako, tādisaṃ uḷāraguṇaṃ āsajja ghaṭṭayitvā ekantakāḷakehi pāpadhammehi samannāgatattā kaṇha māra āyatiṃ mahādukkhaṃ vindissasi.

513. Having struck and beaten. These generate individual feelings of pain, each producing great suffering. 'Ayato apagato nirayo' means hell, that from which good fortune has departed; this should be explained by the Devadūta Sutta (MN 3.261). But its meaning and explanation will come later by itself. However, bringing up this past event, the Great Elder, intimidating Māra by way of revealing the power of his own knowledge, spoke the verse: 'Whoever knows this...' Its meaning is: whoever possesses great knowledge knows this action and its result directly, having made them face him like an āmalaka fruit placed on the palm of the hand. Because the bhikkhu, the chief disciple of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, has completely broken all defilements, and because you, dark Māra, having assailed and struck such magnificent qualities, are endowed with utterly black, evil qualities, you will experience great suffering in the future.

Udakaṃ vatthuṃ katvāti tattha nibbattanakasattānaṃ sādhāraṇakammaphalena mahāsamuddaudakameva adhiṭṭhānaṃ [V 2.0301] katvā. Tathā hi tāni kappaṭṭhitikāni honti. Tenāha “kappaṭṭhāyino”ti. Tesanti vimānānaṃ. Etaṃ yathāvuttavimānavatthuṃ tāsaṃ accharānaṃ sampattiṃ, tassa ca kāraṇaṃ attapaccakkhaṃ katvā jānāti. Pādaṅguṭṭhena kampayīti pubbārāme visākhāya mahāupāsikāya kāritaṃ sahassagabbhapaṭimaṇḍitamahāpāsādaṃ attano pādaṅguṭṭhena kampesi. Tenāha “idaṃ pāsādakampanasuttena dīpetabba”nti. Idanti “yo vejayanta”nti imissā gāthāya atthajātaṃ cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttisutteneva (ma. ni. 1.393) dīpetabbaṃ.

Having made water the foundation: having established the great ocean's water itself as the basis, as a result of the common kamma of the beings born there. Indeed, they last for an eon. Hence it is said, 'lasting for an eon.' 'Theirs'—referring to the celestial mansions. He knows firsthand the splendor of those nymphs belonging to the aforesaid celestial mansion and the reason for it. He shook it with his big toe: he shook with his big toe the great palace, adorned with a thousand chambers, built by the great lay follower Visākhā in the Eastern Monastery. Hence it is said, 'this should be explained by the Pāsādakampana Sutta.' 'This'—the meaning of the verse beginning 'whoever shakes the Vejayanta Palace' should be explained just by the Cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayavimutti Sutta (MN 1.393).

Tassa brahmagaṇassa tathācintanasamanantarameva tasmiṃ brahmaloke sudhammaṃ brahmasabhaṃ gantvā. Tepīti mahāmoggallānādayo. Paccekaṃ disāsūti [M 2.0324] mahāmoggallānatthero puratthimadisāyaṃ, mahākassapatthero dakkhiṇadisāyaṃ, mahākappinatthero pacchimadisāyaṃ, anuruddhatthero uttaradisāyanti evaṃ cattāro therā brahmaparisamatthake majjhe nisinnassa bhagavato samantato catuddisā nisīdiṃsu. Gāthā vuttāti “yo brahmaṃ paripucchatī”ti gāthā vuttā. Aññatarabrahmasuttenāti – “tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa brahmuno evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hotī”tiādinā (saṃ. ni. 1.176) mahāvagge āgatena aññatarabrahmasuttena.

Immediately after that group of Brahmās thought thus, they went to the Sudhammā assembly hall in that Brahmā world. 'They too'—referring to Mahāmoggallāna and others. In each direction: the elder Mahāmoggallāna in the eastern direction, the elder Mahākassapa in the southern direction, the elder Mahākappina in the western direction, and the elder Anuruddha in the northern direction. Thus, the four elders sat in the four directions around the Blessed One, who was seated in the middle, above the Brahmā assembly. The verse was spoken: that is, the verse 'Who questions Brahmā?' was spoken. By the Aññatarabrahma Sutta: that is, by the Aññatarabrahma Sutta in the Mahāvagga (SN 1.176) beginning, 'At that time, to a certain Brahmā, such an evil viewpoint arose...'

Jhānavimokkhena phusīti jhānavimokkhasannissayena abhiññāñāṇena phassayi. Vananti jambudīpaṃ aphassayīti sambandho. Jambudīpo hi vanabahulatāya idha “vana”nti vutto. Tenāha “jambusaṇḍassa issaro”ti. Pubbavidehānaṃ dīpanti pubbavidehavāsīnaṃ dīpaṃ, pubbavidehadīpanti attho. Bhūmisayā narā nāma aparagoyānakā uttarakurukā ca. Yasmā te gehapariggahābhāvato bhūmiyaṃyeva sayanti, na pāsādādīsu. Paṭilabhīti uppādesi. Etaṃ āsaṃ mā akāsīti esā yathā pubbe dūsimārassa, evaṃ tuyhaṃ āsā dīgharattaṃ anatthāvahā, tasmā edisaṃ āsaṃ mā akāsīti mārassa ovādaṃ adāsi. Sesaṃ sabbattha suviññeyyameva.

He touched with jhāna-liberation: he touched with the knowledge of direct knowing supported by jhāna-liberation. The forest: the connection is that he touched Jambudīpa. Jambudīpa is called 'forest' here because it is abundant with forests. Hence it is said, 'the lord of the Jambu grove.' The island of the Eastern Videhans: the island of those dwelling in Eastern Videha, meaning the Eastern Videha island. The people called Bhūmisayā are the Aparagoyānakas and the Uttarakurus. Because they, lacking houses and possessions, sleep directly on the ground, not in palaces or the like. He obtained: he produced. 'May you not make such a hope': just as for the former Māra Dūsī, so too your hope will bring harm for a long time. Therefore, he gave Māra the advice: 'Do not make such a hope.' The rest is quite easy to understand everywhere.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Of the Papañcasūdanī, the Commentary on the Majjhima Nikāya

Māratajjanīyasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Elucidation of the Hidden Meaning in the Commentary on the Māratajjanīya Sutta is complete.

Niṭṭhitā ca cūḷayamakavaggavaṇṇanā.

And the commentary on the Cūḷayamaka Vagga is finished.

Mūlapaṇṇāsaṭīkā samattā.

The Subcommentary on the Root Fifty is complete.

Dutiyo bhāgo niṭṭhito.

The second part is finished.
